## Forms of Indian theatre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Theatre_of_India&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Forms of Indian theatre")]

### Traditional Indian theatre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Theatre_of_India&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Traditional Indian theatre")]

Main article: [List of traditional Indian theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_traditional_Indian_theatre "List of traditional Indian theatre")

[Kutiyattam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutiyattam "Kutiyattam") is the only surviving specimen of the ancient Sanskrit theatre, thought to have originated around the beginning of the [Common Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Era "Common Era"), and is officially recognised by [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO") as a [Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masterpiece_of_the_Oral_and_Intangible_Heritage_of_Humanity "Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity"). In addition, many forms of Indian folk theatre abound. [Bhavai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhavai "Bhavai") (strolling players) is a popular folk theatre form of [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat"), said to have arisen in the 14th century AD. [Bhaona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhaona "Bhaona") and [Ankiya Nats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankiya_Nat "Ankiya Nat") have been practicing in [Assam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assam "Assam") since the early 16th century which were created and initiated by [Mahapurusha Srimanta Sankardeva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahapurusha_Srimanta_Sankardeva "Mahapurusha Srimanta Sankardeva"). [Jatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jatra_(Bengal) "Jatra (Bengal)") has been popular in [Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal "Bengal") and its origin is traced to the Bhakti movement in the 16th century. Another folk theatre form popular in [Haryana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haryana "Haryana"), Uttar Pradesh and [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") region of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh") is [Swang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swang_(dance_drama) "Swang (dance drama)"), which is dialogue-oriented rather than movement-oriented and is considered to have arisen in its present form in the late 18th – early 19th centuries.

[Yakshagana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakshagana "Yakshagana") is a very popular theatre art in Karnataka and has existed under different names at least since the 16th century. It is semi-classical in nature and involves music and songs based on [carnatic music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnatic_music "Carnatic music"), rich costumes, storylines based on the _[Mahabharata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahabharata "Mahabharata")_ and _[Ramayana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramayana "Ramayana")._ It also employs spoken dialogue in-between its songs that gives it a [folk art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_art "Folk art") flavour. [Kathakali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathakali "Kathakali") is a form of dance-drama, characteristic of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), that arose in the 17th century, developing from the temple-art plays [Krishnanattam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishnanattam "Krishnanattam") and [Ramanattam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanattam "Ramanattam").

### Urdu/Hindustani theatre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Theatre_of_India&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Urdu/Hindustani theatre")]

Urdu drama evolved from the prevailing dramatic traditions of North India shaping Rahas or Raas as practiced by exponents like [Wajid Ali Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wajid_Ali_Shah "Wajid Ali Shah"), [Nawab of Awadh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nawab_of_Awadh "Nawab of Awadh"). His dramatic experiments led to the famous _[Inder Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inder\_Sabha "Inder Sabha")_ of [Agha Hasan Amanat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agha_Hasan_Amanat "Agha Hasan Amanat"), and later this tradition took the shape of [Parsi theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parsi_theatre "Parsi theatre"). _[Yahudi Ki Ladki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahudi\_Ki\_Ladki "Yahudi Ki Ladki")_ (_The Jew's Daughter_) by [Agha Hashar Kashmiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agha_Hashar_Kashmiri "Agha Hashar Kashmiri") is the culmination of this tradition.

Among all the languages Urdu (which was called Hindi by early writers), along with Gujrati, Marathi and Bengali theatres have kept flourishing and demand for its writers and artists has not subsided by the drama aficionados. All the early gems of Urdu theatre (performed by Parsi Companies) were made into films. Great works like those by Shakespeare have influenced modern Urdu tradition to a large extent when Indian, Iranian, Turkish stories and folk was adapted for stage with heavy doses of Urdu poetry. In modern times writers like [Imtiaz Ali Taj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imtiaz_Ali_Taj "Imtiaz Ali Taj"), Rafi Peer, Krishan Chander, Manto, Upender Nath Ashk, Ghulam Rabbani, Prof. Mujeeb and many others shaped this tradition.

While Prof Hasan, Ghulam Jeelani, J.N. Kaushal, Shameem Hanfi, Jameel Shaidayi etc. belong to the old generation, contemporary writers like Mujeeb Khan, [Javed Siddiqui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Siddiqui "Javed Siddiqui"), Sayeed Alam, Danish Iqbal, Anis Azmi, Aftab Hasnain, Aslam Parvez, Anis Javed, Iqbal Niyazi, [Syed Sahil Agha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syed_Sahil_Agha "Syed Sahil Agha") and Zaheer Anwar are postmodern playwrights actively contributing in the field of Urdu drama.

Zaheer Anwar has kept the flag of Urdu theatre flying in Kolkata. Unlike the writers of previous generations, Danish iqbal and Zaheer do not write bookish plays but their work is a product of a vigorous performing tradition. Iqbal Niyazi of Mumbai has written several plays in Urdu. His play _Aur Kitne Jalyanwala BaughU??_ won a national award and other awards. Hence this is the only generation after Amanat and Agha Hashr who actually write for the stage and not for libraries.

The group Aatrangi Pitaara Foundation is actively performing and saving Hindustani theatre. Their presentation of _Anti-National Ghalib_,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_theatre#cite_note-35) written by Danish Iqbal, has been well received by the Delhi Theatre enthusiasts. Leading the group, [Keshav Raina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keshav_Raina?action=edit&redlink=1 "Keshav Raina (page does not exist)") is developing more Hindustani shows showcasing the rich history and heritage of India.

### Indian puppet theatre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Theatre_of_India&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Indian puppet theatre")]

[Yakshagana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakshagana "Yakshagana") is a popular semi-classical theatre art from coastal Karnataka. It uses rich costumes, music, dance, and dialogue. Puppet shows in parts of Karnataka uses all these elements of [yakshagana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakshagana "Yakshagana") to depict stories from the _[Ramayana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramayana "Ramayana")_ and _[Mahabharata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahabharata "Mahabharata")._

### Mobile theatre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Theatre_of_India&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Mobile theatre")]

Mobile theatres are a kind of popular theatre form that exist mainly in [Assam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assam "Assam").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] For staging their plays, theatre groups travel different places with their casts, singers, musicians, dancers and entire crew. Even the tent and chairs for the audience are carried with them. Mobile theatre was first staged on 2 October 1963 in [Pathsala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathsala "Pathsala"), Assam. [Achyut Lahkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achyut_Lahkar "Achyut Lahkar") is known as the father of mobile theatre.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_theatre#cite_note-36)

**Anupam Kher** (born 7 March 1955) is an [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India") actor, director and producer who works primarily in [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema"). In a career spanning over four decades, he has acted in more than [540 films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher_filmography "Anupam Kher filmography"). A veteran of Indian cinema,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-actorsprep-1) Kher is recipient of two [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") and eight [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards") for his acting performances.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-2)[Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") awarded him the [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") in 2004[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-3) and the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") in 2016[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-4) for his contribution to Indian cinema and arts.

Kher made his acting debut with [Mahesh Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahesh_Bhatt "Mahesh Bhatt")-directed drama film _[Saaransh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saaransh "Saaransh")_[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-5) (1984), which marked Kher's breakthrough role, earning him the [Filmfare Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Actor") for his portrayal of an elderly father. Since then he starred in several other supporting roles. He was appreciated in negative roles in films such as _[Karma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karma\_(1986\_film) "Karma (1986 film)")_ (1986), _[Tezaab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tezaab "Tezaab")_ (1988) and _[ChaalBaaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChaalBaaz "ChaalBaaz")_ (1989). For _[Vijay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijay\_(1988\_film) "Vijay (1988 film)")_ (1988), he won the [Filmfare Best Supporting Actor Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Best_Supporting_Actor_Award "Filmfare Best Supporting Actor Award") for his performance. In 1989, _[Ram Lakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram\_Lakhan "Ram Lakhan")_ garnered him wider recognition for his comic performances and won him [Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Comic Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_a_Comic_Role "Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Comic Role"), and for _[Daddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daddy\_(1989\_film) "Daddy (1989 film)")_, he won a[National Film Award – Special Jury Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_%E2%80%93_Special_Jury_Award_(feature_film) "National Film Award – Special Jury Award (feature film)")and[Filmfare Critics Award for Best Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Critics_Award_for_Best_Performance "Filmfare Critics Award for Best Performance"). In later years, Kher was nominated for [Filmfare Best Supporting Actor Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Best_Supporting_Actor_Award "Filmfare Best Supporting Actor Award") for _[Dil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_(1990\_film) "Dil (1990 film)")_ (1990), _[Saudagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudagar\_(1991\_film) "Saudagar (1991 film)")_ (1991), _[Lamhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamhe "Lamhe")_ (1991), _[Hum Aapke Hain Koun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hum\_Aapke\_Hain\_Koun "Hum Aapke Hain Koun")_ (1994), _[Chaahat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaahat\_(1996\_film) "Chaahat (1996 film)")_ (1996), _[Special 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special\_26 "Special 26")_ (2013) and _[Uunchai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uunchai "Uunchai")_ (2022).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-6) He was nominated in the category of [Filmfare Award for Best Comedian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_a_Comic_Role "Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Comic Role") for films, such as _[Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Hai\_Ke\_Manta\_Nahin "Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin")_ (1991), _[Shola Aur Shabnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shola\_Aur\_Shabnam\_(1992\_film) "Shola Aur Shabnam (1992 film)")_ (1992), _[Kuch Kuch Hota Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuch\_Kuch\_Hota\_Hai "Kuch Kuch Hota Hai")_ (1998), _[Dulhan Hum Le Jayenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulhan\_Hum\_Le\_Jayenge "Dulhan Hum Le Jayenge")_ (2000), and won for _[Khel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khel\_(1992\_film) "Khel (1992 film)")_ (1992), _[Darr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darr "Darr")_ (1993) and _[Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilwale\_Dulhania\_Le\_Jayenge "Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge")_ (1995).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-7)

Kher's other acclaimed roles include _[Khosla Ka Ghosla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khosla\_Ka\_Ghosla "Khosla Ka Ghosla")_ (2006), _[Buddha Mar Gaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddha\_Mar\_Gaya "Buddha Mar Gaya")_ (2006), _[A Wednesday!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Wednesday! "A Wednesday!")_ (2008), _[Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby\_(2015\_Hindi\_film) "Baby (2015 Hindi film)")_ (2015), _[M. S. Dhoni: The Untold Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.\_S.\_Dhoni:\_The\_Untold\_Story "M. S. Dhoni: The Untold Story")_ (2016), _[The Kashmir Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Kashmir\_Files "The Kashmir Files")_ (2022) and _[Metro... In Dino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro...\_In\_Dino "Metro... In Dino")_ (2025).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-News18-9) Besides working in Hindi films, he has also appeared in international films such as the [Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe "Golden Globe")-nominated _[Bend It Like Beckham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bend\_It\_Like\_Beckham "Bend It Like Beckham")_ (2002), [Ang Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Lee "Ang Lee")'s [Golden Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Lion "Golden Lion")-winning [NC-17 rated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NC-17_rated_films "List of NC-17 rated films")_[Lust, Caution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lust,\_Caution "Lust, Caution")_ (2007), [David O. Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_O._Russell "David O. Russell")'s [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")-winning _[Silver Linings Playbook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver\_Linings\_Playbook "Silver Linings Playbook")_ (2012) and Anthony Maras' _[Hotel Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel\_Mumbai "Hotel Mumbai")_ (2019). He received a [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA "BAFTA") nomination for his supporting role in the British television film _[The Boy with the Topknot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boy\_with\_the\_Topknot "The Boy with the Topknot")_ (2018).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:0-10) Anupam Kher will portray [Rabindranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabindranath_Tagore "Rabindranath Tagore") in his 538th film.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-11)

He has previously served as the Chairman of the [Central Board of Film Certification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Board_of_Film_Certification "Central Board of Film Certification") and the [National School of Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_School_of_Drama "National School of Drama") in India.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:1-12) Kher was appointed Chairman of the [Film and Television Institute of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_and_Television_Institute_of_India "Film and Television Institute of India") (FTII) in October 2017.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-13) His appointment was [controversial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Controversial "Controversial"), given his support for the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:3-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-17) A year later, he resigned as the chairman of the FTII, citing his work commitments for the American TV show _[New Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Amsterdam\_(2018\_TV\_series) "New Amsterdam (2018 TV series)")_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-18)

## Early life and background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anupam_Kher&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and background")]

Anupam Kher was born on 7 March 1955 in [Simla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimla "Shimla"), in the ertswhile [Patiala and East Punjab States Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patiala_and_East_Punjab_States_Union "Patiala and East Punjab States Union") of India (now in [Himachal Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himachal_Pradesh "Himachal Pradesh")), into a [Kashmiri Pandit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmiri_Pandit "Kashmiri Pandit") family.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-DOB-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-20) His father, Pushkar Nath Kher was a clerk in the forest department of [Himachal Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himachal_Pradesh "Himachal Pradesh") and his mother, Dulari Kher was a housewife.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-22) He was educated at D. A. V. School in Shimla.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-23) He studied economics at [Government College, Sanjauli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_College,_Sanjauli "Government College, Sanjauli") under [Himachal Pradesh University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himachal_Pradesh_University "Himachal Pradesh University"), [Shimla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimla "Shimla"), but dropped out to study Indian theatre at [Panjab University, Chandigarh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panjab_University,_Chandigarh "Panjab University, Chandigarh").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-24)

In 1978, Kher graduated from the [National School of Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_School_of_Drama "National School of Drama") (NSD) in [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:1-12) Some of his early roles were in plays performed at the Himachal Pradesh University.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-KBHSH-25) He taught drama in [Raj Bisaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Bisaria "Raj Bisaria")'s [Bharatendu Natya Akademi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatendu_Academy_of_Dramatic_Arts "Bharatendu Academy of Dramatic Arts") in [Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucknow,_Uttar_Pradesh "Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh") for a small part in his directorial debut movie _Sheeshay ka Ghar_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:3-14)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-26) In his early struggling days as an actor in Bombay (present-day Mumbai), he reportedly slept on a railway platform for a month.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:2-27)

## Acting career

Further information: [Anupam Kher filmography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher_filmography "Anupam Kher filmography")

### Debut and early career (1984–1988)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anupam_Kher&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Debut and early career (1984–1988)")]

Anupam Kher made his acting debut in 1984 with [Mahesh Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahesh_Bhatt "Mahesh Bhatt")'s [drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(genre) "Drama (genre)") film _[Saaransh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saaransh "Saaransh")_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-28) It didn't perform well commercially, but was a huge critical success and was chosen as [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India")'s official entry for the [Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Foreign_Language_Film "Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-FI1984-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-academy-30) Kher received widespread acclaim for his portraying a 60-year-old man trying to come to terms with the loss of his only son and won his first and only [Filmfare Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Actor").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-FA-31) The following year, however, none of his films performed well critically or commercially with [Rahul Rawail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahul_Rawail "Rahul Rawail")'s [action drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_(genre) "Action (genre)")_[Arjun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjun\_(1985\_film) "Arjun (1985 film)")_ co-starring [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol") and [Dimple Kapadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimple_Kapadia "Dimple Kapadia") being the exception.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-32) This changed in 1986 when he co-starred alongside [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") in [K. Bhagyaraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Bhagyaraj "K. Bhagyaraj")'s [crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_drama "Crime drama")_[Aakhree Raasta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aakhree\_Raasta "Aakhree Raasta")_ and played the ruthless villain "Dr. Michael Dang" in [Subhash Ghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subhash_Ghai "Subhash Ghai")'s ensemble actioner _[Karma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karma\_(1986\_film) "Karma (1986 film)")_, which had [Dilip Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar"), [Jackie Shroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff"), [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor"), [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah") and [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi") in the lead.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-34) While the former was a hit, _Karma_ went on to become a blockbuster and Kher was noticed by the audience.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-TG1986-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-36) The same year, he played supporting role in another major commercial success, which was - _[Insaaf Ki Awaaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insaaf\_Ki\_Awaaz "Insaaf Ki Awaaz")_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-TG1986-35)

In 1987, he appeared alongside [Rekha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rekha "Rekha") and [Raj Babbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Babbar "Raj Babbar") in [T. Rama Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._Rama_Rao "T. Rama Rao")'s family drama _[Sansar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sansar\_(1987\_film) "Sansar (1987 film)")_, which was a commercially successful venture.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-37) In 1988, he played negative roles in films, such as _[Hatya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatya "Hatya")_, _[Zakhmi Aurat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakhmi\_Aurat "Zakhmi Aurat")_ and _[Tezaab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tezaab "Tezaab")_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-39) Out of these releases, _Hatya_ and _Zakhmi Aurat_ were semi-hits, while the lattermost went many steps ahead and emerged a blockbuster as well as the [highest earning film of that year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Indian_films_of_1988 "List of Indian films of 1988").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-40) Kher's other notable release of 1988, _Vijay_ failed at the box office, but won him his first and only [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-filmfare-awards-41)

### Breakthrough, public recognition and awards success (1989–2001)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anupam_Kher&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Breakthrough, public recognition and awards success (1989–2001)")]

After many years of lukewarm critical and commercial success, Kher became a household name in 1989 when he starred in Subhash Ghai's [masala film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masala_film "Masala film")_[Ram Lakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram\_Lakhan "Ram Lakhan")_, [Rajiv Rai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajiv_Rai "Rajiv Rai")'s action drama _[Tridev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tridev "Tridev")_, [Yash Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yash_Chopra "Yash Chopra")'s [romantic musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film")_[Chandni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandni\_(1989\_film) "Chandni (1989 film)")_, [Vidhu Vinod Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vidhu_Vinod_Chopra "Vidhu Vinod Chopra")'s crime drama _[Parinda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parinda "Parinda")_ and [Pankaj Parashar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pankaj_Parashar "Pankaj Parashar")'s [comedy drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_(genre) "Comedy (genre)")_[ChaalBaaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChaalBaaz "ChaalBaaz")_. All the films proved to be critically and commercially successful, especially _Ram Lakhan_, _Tridev_ and _Chandni_, all three of which backed up with chartbuster music, emerged blockbusters at the box office and were among the top five highest-grossing films of the year.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-43) Apart from commercial projects, Kher also collaborated with Mahesh Bhatt for the art-house [television film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television "Television")_[Daddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daddy\_(1989\_film) "Daddy (1989 film)")_, which like their previous collaboration _Saaransh_ met with immense acclaim and won Kher his first [National Film Award – Special Jury Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_%E2%80%93_Special_Jury_Award_(feature_film) "National Film Award – Special Jury Award (feature film)") as well as [Filmfare Award for Best Actor (Critics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Critics_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Critics Award for Best Actor").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-HTJune-45) The following year, he starred in [Indra Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indra_Kumar "Indra Kumar")'s blockbuster [romantic comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film")_[Dil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_(1990\_film) "Dil (1990 film)")_, which had [Aamir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") and [Madhuri Dixit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhuri_Dixit "Madhuri Dixit") in the lead roles.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-46) For his performance of a greedy father in _Dil_, Kher received his third nomination in the [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor") category.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-FA-31) In 1991, he appeared in highly successful films, including _[Saudagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudagar\_(1991\_film) "Saudagar (1991 film)")_, _[Saathi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saathi\_(1991\_film) "Saathi (1991 film)")_, _[Hum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hum\_(1991\_film) "Hum (1991 film)")_ and _[Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Hai\_Ke\_Manta\_Nahin "Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin")_.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-47) He also collaborated with Yash Chopra for the romantic drama _[Lamhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamhe\_(1991\_film) "Lamhe (1991 film)")_, which was a commercial failure, but received positive reception from critics and is now considered a cult classic.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-49) Kher's performances in _Saudagar_ and _Lamhe_ earned him nomination in the [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor") category.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-Filmfare-50)

His other box office hits of this period, include _[Beta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta\_(film) "Beta (film)")_ (1992), _[Shola Aur Shabnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shola\_Aur\_Shabnam\_(1992\_film) "Shola Aur Shabnam (1992 film)")_ (1992), _[Lootere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lootere "Lootere")_ (1993), _[Waqt Hamara Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waqt\_Hamara\_Hai "Waqt Hamara Hai")_ (1993), _[Khalnayak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalnayak "Khalnayak")_ (1993), _[Hum Hain Kamaal Ke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hum\_Hain\_Kamaal\_Ke "Hum Hain Kamaal Ke")_ (1993), _[Gumrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gumrah\_(1993\_film) "Gumrah (1993 film)")_ (1993) and _[Darr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darr "Darr")_ (1993).[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-Filmography-51) He then appeared in [Sooraj Barjatya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sooraj_Barjatya "Sooraj Barjatya")'s _[Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hum\_Aapke\_Hain\_Koun..! "Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!")_ (1994) and [Aditya Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aditya_Chopra "Aditya Chopra")'s _[Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilwale\_Dulhania\_Le\_Jayenge "Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge")_ (1995).[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-toi800-52) Both the films did extremely well at the box office and emerged _All Time Blockbusters_ as well as the highest and second highest-grossing film of all time, respectively.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-54) For his performance in the former, Kher received another nomination in the [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor") category.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-Film-55) In the late-1990s, he continued to play supporting roles commercially successful ventures, such as _[Judwaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judwaa "Judwaa")_ (1997), _[Ziddi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziddi\_(1997\_film) "Ziddi (1997 film)")_ (1997), _[Deewana Mastana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deewana\_Mastana "Deewana Mastana")_ (1997), _[Kuch Kuch Hota Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuch\_Kuch\_Hota\_Hai "Kuch Kuch Hota Hai")_ (1998), _[Bade Miyan Chote Miyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bade\_Miyan\_Chote\_Miyan\_(1998\_film) "Bade Miyan Chote Miyan (1998 film)")_ (1998), _[Hum Aapke Dil Mein Rehte Hain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hum\_Aapke\_Dil\_Mein\_Rehte\_Hain "Hum Aapke Dil Mein Rehte Hain")_ (1999) and _[Haseena Maan Jaayegi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haseena\_Maan\_Jaayegi "Haseena Maan Jaayegi")_ (1999).[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-Filmography-51)

Kher began the new decade playing an antagonist in [Rakesh Roshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakesh_Roshan "Rakesh Roshan")'s [romantic blockbuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film")_[Kaho Naa... Pyaar Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaho\_Naa...\_Pyaar\_Hai "Kaho Naa... Pyaar Hai")_ which made [Hrithik Roshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrithik_Roshan "Hrithik Roshan") a star.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-57) He followed it with four more major successes the same year with _[Dulhan Hum Le Jayenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulhan\_Hum\_Le\_Jayenge "Dulhan Hum Le Jayenge")_, _[Kya Kehna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kya\_Kehna "Kya Kehna")_, _[Hamara Dil Aapke Paas Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamara\_Dil\_Aapke\_Paas\_Hai "Hamara Dil Aapke Paas Hai")_ and _[Mohabbatein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohabbatein "Mohabbatein")_.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-Filmography-51) In 2001, he had another hit in _[Jodi No.1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodi\_No.1\_(film) "Jodi No.1 (film)")_ and received praise for his performance in _[Rehnaa Hai Terre Dil Mein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rehnaa\_Hai\_Terre\_Dil\_Mein "Rehnaa Hai Terre Dil Mein")_, which did not do well commercially, but went on to attain cult status in later years.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-Filmography-51)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-58)

### Expansion to Hollywood and further acclaim (2002–2018)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anupam_Kher&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Expansion to Hollywood and further acclaim (2002–2018)")]

In 2002, Kher starred in his first [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States") project which was [Gurinder Chadha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurinder_Chadha "Gurinder Chadha")'s [sports comedy drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_film "Sport film")_[Bend It Like Beckham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bend\_It\_Like\_Beckham "Bend It Like Beckham")_.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-59) The film proved to be a critical and commercial success grossing around $76.6 million worldwide.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-61) A year later, he reunited with Chadha for _[Bride and Prejudice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bride\_and\_Prejudice "Bride and Prejudice")_, which too was a successful venture.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-62) His final collaboration with Chadha took place in 2005 for _[The Mistress of Spices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mistress\_of\_Spices "The Mistress of Spices")_, which had [Aishwarya Rai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aishwarya_Rai "Aishwarya Rai") and [Dylan McDermott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_McDermott "Dylan McDermott") in the lead and unlike their previous ventures was panned by critics and did not do well.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-64)

During this period, Kher continued to star in notable Hindi films, such as _[Veer-Zaara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veer-Zaara "Veer-Zaara")_ (2004), _[Kyaa Kool Hain Hum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyaa\_Kool\_Hain\_Hum "Kyaa Kool Hain Hum")_ (2005) and received immense acclaim and his second [National Film Award – Special Jury Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_%E2%80%93_Special_Jury_Award_(feature_film) "National Film Award – Special Jury Award (feature film)") for the 2005 film _[Maine Gandhi Ko Nahin Mara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine\_Gandhi\_Ko\_Nahin\_Mara "Maine Gandhi Ko Nahin Mara")_ (which he also produced).[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-Filmography-51)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-auto-65) In the latter-half of the 2000s, he appeared in critically and commercially successful [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") films, including _[Rang De Basanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rang\_De\_Basanti "Rang De Basanti")_ (2006), _[Chup Chup Ke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chup\_Chup\_Ke "Chup Chup Ke")_ (2006), _[Vivah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivah "Vivah")_ (2006), _[Khosla Ka Ghosla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khosla\_Ka\_Ghosla "Khosla Ka Ghosla")_ (2006), _[Apna Sapna Money Money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apna\_Sapna\_Money\_Money "Apna Sapna Money Money")_ (2006), _[A Wednesday!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Wednesday! "A Wednesday!")_ (2008), _[Wake Up Sid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake\_Up\_Sid "Wake Up Sid")_ (2009) and made his [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_China "Cinema of China") film debut with _[Lust, Caution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lust,\_Caution "Lust, Caution")_ (2007), which too was a box office hit grossing around $67.1 million.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-66)

In the following decade, Kher did films of varied genres and found box office success in _[Dabangg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dabangg "Dabangg")_ (2010), _[Yamla Pagla Deewana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamla\_Pagla\_Deewana "Yamla Pagla Deewana")_ (2011), _[Kya Super Kool Hain Hum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kya\_Super\_Kool\_Hain\_Hum "Kya Super Kool Hain Hum")_ (2012), _[Chashme Baddoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chashme\_Baddoor\_(2013\_film) "Chashme Baddoor (2013 film)")_ (2013), _[Singham Returns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singham\_Returns "Singham Returns")_ (2014), _[Prem Ratan Dhan Payo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem\_Ratan\_Dhan\_Payo "Prem Ratan Dhan Payo")_ (2015), _[M.S. Dhoni: The Untold Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.S.\_Dhoni:\_The\_Untold\_Story "M.S. Dhoni: The Untold Story")_ (2016), _[Toilet: Ek Prem Katha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toilet:\_Ek\_Prem\_Katha "Toilet: Ek Prem Katha")_ (2017) and _[Judwaa 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judwaa\_2 "Judwaa 2")_ (2017).[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-Filmography-51) He also received praise for his performances in _[Special 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special\_26 "Special 26")_ (2013), _[Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby\_(2015\_Hindi\_film) "Baby (2015 Hindi film)")_ (2015), _[Indu Sarkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indu\_Sarkar "Indu Sarkar")_ (2017) and _[Love Sonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Sonia "Love Sonia")_ (2018). For _Special 26_, he received a nomination in the Best Supporting Actor category at [59th Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Filmfare_Awards "59th Filmfare Awards").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-67) During this period, he also made his [Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam "Malayalam") film debut with [Blessy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blessy "Blessy")'s _[Pranayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pranayam\_(2011\_film) "Pranayam (2011 film)")_ (2011), played supporting roles in blockbuster Hollywood ventures, including [David O. Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_O._Russell "David O. Russell")'s _[Silver Linings Playbook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver\_Linings\_Playbook "Silver Linings Playbook")_ (2012) and [Michael Showalter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Showalter "Michael Showalter")'s _[The Big Sick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Big\_Sick "The Big Sick")_ (2017) and received a nomination in the [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA "BAFTA")[Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "British Academy Television Award for Best Supporting Actor") category for his performance in Lynsey Miller's _[The Boy With The Topknot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boy\_With\_The\_Topknot "The Boy With The Topknot")_ (2017).[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-70)

### Work in regional industries and continued success (2019–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anupam_Kher&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Work in regional industries and continued success (2019–present)")]

In 2019, Kher played the role of former [PM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister "Prime Minister")[Manmohan Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manmohan_Singh "Manmohan Singh") in _[The Accidental Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Accidental\_Prime\_Minister\_(film) "The Accidental Prime Minister (film)")_ and a vigilante in _[One Day: Justice Delivered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_Day:\_Justice\_Delivered "One Day: Justice Delivered")_, both of which were critical and commercial failures.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-72)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-Filmography-51) After a gap of almost 3 years, he returned to the big screen playing one of the leads in [Vivek Agnihotri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivek_Agnihotri "Vivek Agnihotri")'s _[The Kashmir Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Kashmir\_Files "The Kashmir Files")_ (2022). It received polarising response from critics, but proved to be a huge blockbuster and got Kher a nomination in the Best Actor category at [68th Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/68th_Filmfare_Awards "68th Filmfare Awards").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-Filmography-51)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-73) The same year he appeared in the [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") film _[Karthikeya 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karthikeya\_2 "Karthikeya 2")_, which also emerged a blockbuster at the box office.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-74)

In 2023, he appeared in the successful Malayalam comedy _[Voice of Sathyanathan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voice\_of\_Sathyanathan "Voice of Sathyanathan")_ and [Kannada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannada "Kannada") actioner _[Ghost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost\_(2023\_film) "Ghost (2023 film)")_, which too did well.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-76) This was followed by a series of box office duds like _[Shiv Shastri Balboa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiv\_Shastri\_Balboa "Shiv Shastri Balboa")_ (2023), _[IB71](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IB71 "IB71")_ (2023), _[The Vaccine War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Vaccine\_War "The Vaccine War")_ (2023), _[Emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency\_(2025\_film) "Emergency (2025 film)")_ (2025) and _[Tumko Meri Kasam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumko\_Meri\_Kasam "Tumko Meri Kasam")_ (2025) with the exception being [Anurag Basu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anurag_Basu "Anurag Basu")'s romantic musical _[Metro In Dino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro\_In\_Dino "Metro In Dino")_ (2025) for which Kher also made his playback debut.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-79)

## Other works

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anupam_Kher&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Other works")]

Kher ventured into directing with _[Om Jai Jagadish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om\_Jai\_Jagadish "Om Jai Jagadish")_ (2002) and has been a producer. He produced and starred in the film _[Maine Gandhi Ko Nahin Mara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine\_Gandhi\_Ko\_Nahin\_Mara "Maine Gandhi Ko Nahin Mara")_ (2005). From October 2003 to October 2004, he served as chairman of the [Indian Film Censor Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Board_of_Film_Certification "Central Board of Film Certification").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-80)

In 2011 Kher released his first book _The Best Thing About You is You!_, which was a best-seller. His biography _Lessons Life Taught Me Unknowingly_ was published on 5 August 2019 by [Penguin Random House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Random_House "Penguin Random House"). In 2020, he wrote _Your Best Day Is Today!_, based on his experiences of the [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") crisis.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-84) Remembering his father on his 9th [death anniversary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_anniversary "Death anniversary"), he presented a poem written by [Lucknow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucknow "Lucknow")-based poet [Pankaj Prasun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pankaj_Prasun "Pankaj Prasun") and posted it on social media.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-85)

Kher hosted TV shows such as _Say Na Something To Anupam Uncle_, _[Sawaal Dus Crore Ka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawaal\_Dus\_Crore\_Ka "Sawaal Dus Crore Ka")_ and _[Lead India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead\_India "Lead India")_. In 2014, Kher has written and starred in a play about his own life called _[Kucch Bhi Ho Sakta Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Anupam\_Kher\_Show\_%E2%80%93\_Kucch\_Bhi\_Ho\_Sakta\_Hai "The Anupam Kher Show – Kucch Bhi Ho Sakta Hai")_, which was directed by [Feroz Abbas Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feroz_Abbas_Khan "Feroz Abbas Khan").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-KBHSH-25)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-86) In 2016, Anupam Kher was a narrator in the [ABP News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABP_News "ABP News") documentary TV series _[Bharatvarsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatvarsh\_(TV\_series) "Bharatvarsh (TV series)")_,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-88) which showcased the journey from [ancient India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outline_of_ancient_India "Outline of ancient India") to the 19th century.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-91) In late 2016, Anupam Kher produced _[Khwaabon Ki Zamin Par](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khwaabon\_Ki\_Zamin\_Par "Khwaabon Ki Zamin Par")_, a TV drama airing on [Zindagi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zindagi_(TV_channel) "Zindagi (TV channel)").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-92)

Starting in fall of 2018, Anupam Kher starred in NBC medical drama TV series _[New Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Amsterdam\_(2018\_TV\_series) "New Amsterdam (2018 TV series)")_[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-93) as Dr. Vijay Kapoor (a neurologist). He also appeared as Shahbaz Karim in the [BBC1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC1 "BBC1") drama _[Mrs Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrs\_Wilson "Mrs Wilson")_.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-94) Kher is the founder of Actor Prepares, an acting institute based in Mumbai.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-95)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anupam_Kher&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Kher married actress Madhumati Kapoor in 1979, but divorced after a few years.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-96) In 1985, he married actress [Kirron Kher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirron_Kher "Kirron Kher")[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-97) who is a [Member of Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament,_Lok_Sabha "Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha") from [Chandigarh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandigarh "Chandigarh"), belonging to the [BJP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BJP "BJP").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-TOI-99) Her son, his stepson, is actor [Sikandar Kher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikandar_Kher "Sikandar Kher").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-100) In 2010, he was appointed as the goodwill ambassador of the [Pratham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pratham "Pratham") Education Foundation, which strives to improve children's education in India.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-Anupam_Kher_tells_us_about_his_new_role-101) Kher is an ardent supporter of the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") (BJP) and Indian prime minister [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:3-14)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-102)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-103)

On 20 September 2021, Kher was awarded an [honorary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_degree "Honorary degree")[doctorate degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctorate_degree "Doctorate degree") in [Philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy "Philosophy") of [Hindu Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Studies "Hindu Studies") by the [Hindu University of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_University_of_America "Hindu University of America").[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-104)

**Anupam Kher** (born 7 March 1955) is an [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India") actor, director and producer who works primarily in [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema"). In a career spanning over four decades, he has acted in more than [540 films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher_filmography "Anupam Kher filmography"). A veteran of Indian cinema,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-actorsprep-1) Kher is recipient of two [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") and eight [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards") for his acting performances.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-2)[Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") awarded him the [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") in 2004[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-3) and the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") in 2016[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-4) for his contribution to Indian cinema and arts.

Kher made his acting debut with [Mahesh Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahesh_Bhatt "Mahesh Bhatt")-directed drama film _[Saaransh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saaransh "Saaransh")_[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-5) (1984), which marked Kher's breakthrough role, earning him the [Filmfare Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Actor") for his portrayal of an elderly father. Since then he starred in several other supporting roles. He was appreciated in negative roles in films such as _[Karma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karma\_(1986\_film) "Karma (1986 film)")_ (1986), _[Tezaab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tezaab "Tezaab")_ (1988) and _[ChaalBaaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChaalBaaz "ChaalBaaz")_ (1989). For _[Vijay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijay\_(1988\_film) "Vijay (1988 film)")_ (1988), he won the [Filmfare Best Supporting Actor Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Best_Supporting_Actor_Award "Filmfare Best Supporting Actor Award") for his performance. In 1989, _[Ram Lakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram\_Lakhan "Ram Lakhan")_ garnered him wider recognition for his comic performances and won him [Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Comic Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_a_Comic_Role "Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Comic Role"), and for _[Daddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daddy\_(1989\_film) "Daddy (1989 film)")_, he won a[National Film Award – Special Jury Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_%E2%80%93_Special_Jury_Award_(feature_film) "National Film Award – Special Jury Award (feature film)")and[Filmfare Critics Award for Best Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Critics_Award_for_Best_Performance "Filmfare Critics Award for Best Performance"). In later years, Kher was nominated for [Filmfare Best Supporting Actor Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Best_Supporting_Actor_Award "Filmfare Best Supporting Actor Award") for _[Dil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_(1990\_film) "Dil (1990 film)")_ (1990), _[Saudagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudagar\_(1991\_film) "Saudagar (1991 film)")_ (1991), _[Lamhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamhe "Lamhe")_ (1991), _[Hum Aapke Hain Koun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hum\_Aapke\_Hain\_Koun "Hum Aapke Hain Koun")_ (1994), _[Chaahat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaahat\_(1996\_film) "Chaahat (1996 film)")_ (1996), _[Special 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special\_26 "Special 26")_ (2013) and _[Uunchai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uunchai "Uunchai")_ (2022).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-6) He was nominated in the category of [Filmfare Award for Best Comedian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_a_Comic_Role "Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Comic Role") for films, such as _[Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Hai\_Ke\_Manta\_Nahin "Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin")_ (1991), _[Shola Aur Shabnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shola\_Aur\_Shabnam\_(1992\_film) "Shola Aur Shabnam (1992 film)")_ (1992), _[Kuch Kuch Hota Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuch\_Kuch\_Hota\_Hai "Kuch Kuch Hota Hai")_ (1998), _[Dulhan Hum Le Jayenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulhan\_Hum\_Le\_Jayenge "Dulhan Hum Le Jayenge")_ (2000), and won for _[Khel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khel\_(1992\_film) "Khel (1992 film)")_ (1992), _[Darr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darr "Darr")_ (1993) and _[Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilwale\_Dulhania\_Le\_Jayenge "Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge")_ (1995).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-7)

He has previously served as the Chairman of the [Central Board of Film Certification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Board_of_Film_Certification "Central Board of Film Certification") and the [National School of Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_School_of_Drama "National School of Drama") in India.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:1-12) Kher was appointed Chairman of the [Film and Television Institute of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_and_Television_Institute_of_India "Film and Television Institute of India") (FTII) in October 2017.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-13) His appointment was [controversial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Controversial "Controversial"), given his support for the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:3-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-17) A year later, he resigned as the chairman of the FTII, citing his work commitments for the American TV show _[New Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Amsterdam\_(2018\_TV\_series) "New Amsterdam (2018 TV series)")_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-18)

## Early life and background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anupam_Kher&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and background")]

Anupam Kher was born on 7 March 1955 in [Simla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimla "Shimla"), in the ertswhile [Patiala and East Punjab States Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patiala_and_East_Punjab_States_Union "Patiala and East Punjab States Union") of India (now in [Himachal Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himachal_Pradesh "Himachal Pradesh")), into a [Kashmiri Pandit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmiri_Pandit "Kashmiri Pandit") family.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-DOB-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-20) His father, Pushkar Nath Kher was a clerk in the forest department of [Himachal Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himachal_Pradesh "Himachal Pradesh") and his mother, Dulari Kher was a housewife.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-22) He was educated at D. A. V. School in Shimla.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-23) He studied economics at [Government College, Sanjauli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_College,_Sanjauli "Government College, Sanjauli") under [Himachal Pradesh University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himachal_Pradesh_University "Himachal Pradesh University"), [Shimla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimla "Shimla"), but dropped out to study Indian theatre at [Panjab University, Chandigarh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panjab_University,_Chandigarh "Panjab University, Chandigarh").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-24)

In 1978, Kher graduated from the [National School of Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_School_of_Drama "National School of Drama") (NSD) in [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:1-12) Some of his early roles were in plays performed at the Himachal Pradesh University.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-KBHSH-25) He taught drama in [Raj Bisaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Bisaria "Raj Bisaria")'s [Bharatendu Natya Akademi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatendu_Academy_of_Dramatic_Arts "Bharatendu Academy of Dramatic Arts") in [Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucknow,_Uttar_Pradesh "Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh") for a small part in his directorial debut movie _Sheeshay ka Ghar_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:3-14)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-26) In his early struggling days as an actor in Bombay (present-day Mumbai), he reportedly slept on a railway platform for a month.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-:2-27)

### Debut and early career (1984–1988)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anupam_Kher&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Debut and early career (1984–1988)")]

Anupam Kher made his acting debut in 1984 with [Mahesh Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahesh_Bhatt "Mahesh Bhatt")'s [drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(genre) "Drama (genre)") film _[Saaransh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saaransh "Saaransh")_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-28) It didn't perform well commercially, but was a huge critical success and was chosen as [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India")'s official entry for the [Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Foreign_Language_Film "Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-FI1984-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-academy-30) Kher received widespread acclaim for his portraying a 60-year-old man trying to come to terms with the loss of his only son and won his first and only [Filmfare Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Actor").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-FA-31) The following year, however, none of his films performed well critically or commercially with [Rahul Rawail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahul_Rawail "Rahul Rawail")'s [action drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_(genre) "Action (genre)")_[Arjun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjun\_(1985\_film) "Arjun (1985 film)")_ co-starring [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol") and [Dimple Kapadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimple_Kapadia "Dimple Kapadia") being the exception.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-32) This changed in 1986 when he co-starred alongside [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") in [K. Bhagyaraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Bhagyaraj "K. Bhagyaraj")'s [crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_drama "Crime drama")_[Aakhree Raasta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aakhree\_Raasta "Aakhree Raasta")_ and played the ruthless villain "Dr. Michael Dang" in [Subhash Ghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subhash_Ghai "Subhash Ghai")'s ensemble actioner _[Karma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karma\_(1986\_film) "Karma (1986 film)")_, which had [Dilip Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar"), [Jackie Shroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff"), [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor"), [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah") and [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi") in the lead.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-34) While the former was a hit, _Karma_ went on to become a blockbuster and Kher was noticed by the audience.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-TG1986-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-36) The same year, he played supporting role in another major commercial success, which was - _[Insaaf Ki Awaaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insaaf\_Ki\_Awaaz "Insaaf Ki Awaaz")_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-TG1986-35)

In 1987, he appeared alongside [Rekha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rekha "Rekha") and [Raj Babbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Babbar "Raj Babbar") in [T. Rama Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._Rama_Rao "T. Rama Rao")'s family drama _[Sansar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sansar\_(1987\_film) "Sansar (1987 film)")_, which was a commercially successful venture.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-37) In 1988, he played negative roles in films, such as _[Hatya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatya "Hatya")_, _[Zakhmi Aurat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakhmi\_Aurat "Zakhmi Aurat")_ and _[Tezaab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tezaab "Tezaab")_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-39) Out of these releases, _Hatya_ and _Zakhmi Aurat_ were semi-hits, while the lattermost went many steps ahead and emerged a blockbuster as well as the [highest earning film of that year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Indian_films_of_1988 "List of Indian films of 1988").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-40) Kher's other notable release of 1988, _Vijay_ failed at the box office, but won him his first and only [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupam_Kher#cite_note-filmfare-awards-41)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anupam_Kher&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Breakthrough, public recognition and awards success (1989–2001)")]

After many years of lukewarm critical and commercial success, Kher became a household name in 1989 when he starred in Subhash Ghai's [masala film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masala_film "Masala film")_[Ram Lakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram\_Lakhan "Ram Lakhan")_, [Rajiv Rai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajiv_Rai "Rajiv Rai")'s action drama _[Tridev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tridev "Tridev")_, [Yash Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yash_Chopra "Yash Chopra")'s [romantic musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film")_[Chandni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandni\_(1989\_film) "Chandni (1989 film)")_, [Vidhu Vinod Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vidhu_Vinod_Chopra "Vidhu Vinod Chopra")'s crime drama _[Parinda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parinda "Parinda")_ and [Pankaj Parashar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pankaj_Parashar "Pankaj Parashar")'s [comedy drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_(genre) "Comedy (genre)")_[ChaalBaaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ChaalBaaz "ChaalBaaz")_.
