**Pran Krishan Sikand** (pronounced[[pra:n]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu"); 12 February 1920 – 12 July 2013), better known [mononymously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mononymous_person "Mononymous person") as **Pran**, was an Indian actor who worked in [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema"). He was one of the most successful and respected actors in the history of [Indian cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cinema "Indian cinema"); in a career spanning over six decades he was also one of the highest-paid actors of his time.

Pran was in/famous for his [villain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villain "Villain") roles, and a highly regarded character actor in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") from the 1940s to the 1990s.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-1) He played heroes from 1940 to 1947, negative roles from 1942 to 1991, and supporting and character roles from 1967 to 2007. From the late 1940s through the 70s was the peak of Pran's career as a villain, especially in the 1950s and 60s: his interpretations were the first true personification of "evil" on the Indian screen, and the intensity of his portrayals of negative/villainous characters was such that the given name "Pran" fell into disuse.

In a long and prolific career, Pran appeared in over [362 films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_filmography "Pran filmography"). He played the leading man in _[Khandaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khandan\_(1942\_film) "Khandan (1942 film)")_ (1942), _Pilpili Saheb_ (1954) and _[Halaku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halaku\_(film) "Halaku (film)")_ (1956), and was known for his roles in _[Madhumati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhumati "Madhumati")_ (1958), _[Jis Desh Mein Ganga Behti Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jis\_Desh\_Mein\_Ganga\_Behti\_Hai "Jis Desh Mein Ganga Behti Hai")_ (1960), _[Shaheed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed\_(1965\_film) "Shaheed (1965 film)")_ (1965), _[Upkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upkar "Upkar")_ (1967), _[Ram Aur Shyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram\_Aur\_Shyam "Ram Aur Shyam")_ (1967), _[Aansoo Ban Gaye Phool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aansoo\_Ban\_Gaye\_Phool "Aansoo Ban Gaye Phool")_ (1969), _[Purab Aur Paschim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purab\_Aur\_Paschim "Purab Aur Paschim")_ (1970), _[Johny Mera Naam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johny\_Mera\_Naam "Johny Mera Naam")_ (1970), _[Victoria No. 203](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria\_No.\_203\_(1972\_film) "Victoria No. 203 (1972 film)")_ (1972), _[Be-Imaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Be-Imaan "Be-Imaan")_ (1972), _[Zanjeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zanjeer\_(1973\_film) "Zanjeer (1973 film)")_ (1973), _[Majboor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majboor\_(1974\_film) "Majboor (1974 film)")_ (1974), _[Amar Akbar Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar\_Akbar\_Anthony "Amar Akbar Anthony")_ (1977), _[Don](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don\_(1978\_film) "Don (1978 film)")_ (1978), _[Sharaabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharaabi "Sharaabi")_ (1984) and _[Duniya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duniya\_(1984\_film) "Duniya (1984 film)")_ (1984).

Pran received many [#Awards and honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#Awards_and_honours) in his career, including the [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor") in 1967, 1969 and 1972, and was awarded the [Filmfare Special Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Special_Award "Filmfare Special Award") in 1997. He was named _"Villain of the Millennium"_ by [Stardust Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stardust_Awards "Stardust Awards") in 2000.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-2) The [Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") honoured him with the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") Award in 2001[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Padma_Awards-3) for his contributions to [the arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_arts "The arts"). He was honoured in 2013 with the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award"), the highest national award for cinema artists, by the Government of India. In 2010, he was named on the list of CNN's Top 25 Asian actors of all time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-5)

Pran died on 12 July 2013 at the age of 93 at Mumbai's [Lilavati Hospital and Research Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilavati_Hospital_and_Research_Centre "Lilavati Hospital and Research Centre") after suffering a prolonged illness.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-6)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Pran was born on 12 February 1920 in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-of-7) into a wealthy [Punjabi Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_Hindu "Punjabi Hindu") family but raised in Ballimaran of [Old Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Delhi "Old Delhi") in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"). His father, Lala Kewal Krishan Sikand,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-8) was a [civil engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_engineer "Civil engineer") and a government civil contractor; his mother was Rameshwari. Pran was one of seven children; four sons and three daughters.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-bol-9)

Pran was academically gifted, especially in mathematics. His father had a transferable job, and so Pran studied in various places, including [Dehradun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehradun "Dehradun"), Lahore, [Kapurthala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapurthala "Kapurthala"), [Meerut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meerut "Meerut") and [Unnao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unnao "Unnao") (Uttar Pradesh), finally completing his [matriculation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matriculation "Matriculation") from Hamid School, in [Rampur (U.P.)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rampur,_Uttar_Pradesh "Rampur, Uttar Pradesh"). After that, he joined A. Das & Co., [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi") as an apprentice to become a professional photographer. He travelled to [Shimla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimla "Shimla") and played [Sita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sita "Sita") in a local staging of "[Ramlila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramlila "Ramlila")". [Madan Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madan_Puri "Madan Puri") enacted the role of [Rama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rama "Rama") in this play.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-10)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career (1940–1967)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career (1940–1967)")]

Pran got his first role in [Dalsukh M. Pancholi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalsukh_M._Pancholi "Dalsukh M. Pancholi")'s [Punjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_language "Punjabi language") film _[Yamla Jat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamla\_Jat "Yamla Jat")_ (1940) because of an accidental meeting with writer Wali Mohammad Wali at a shop in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-11) Directed by Moti B. Gidwani, the film featured [Noor Jehan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noor_Jehan "Noor Jehan") and [Durga Khote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durga_Khote "Durga Khote"). This was followed by small roles in the film _Chaudhary_ and _Khajanchi_, both in 1941. Pancholi cast him again in _[Khandaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khandaan\_(1942\_film) "Khandaan (1942 film)")_ (1942), which was Pran's first [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi")-language film. It featured him as a [romantic hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_hero "Romantic hero"), opposite Noor Jehan, who had acted with him in _Yamla Jat_ as a child artist.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-tri-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-14) In _Khandaan_, she was under 15 years old and compensated for the difference in their heights in [close-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close-up "Close-up") shots by standing on top of bricks.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-15) In the [pre-independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India") era, director Gidwani cast Pran in more films like _Kaise Kahoon_ (1945) and _Khamosh Nigahen_ (1946).

Pran had acted in 22 films from 1942 to 1946 in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore"); 18 were released by 1947. Due to [India's partition in 1947](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India"), his career had a brief break. His films from 1944 to 1947 were made in undivided India, but _Taraash_ (1951) and _Khanabadosh_ (1952) (both co-starring [Manorama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manorama_(Hindi_actress) "Manorama (Hindi actress)")) were released only in Pakistan after Partition. He left Lahore and arrived in [Bombay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay "Bombay"). For a few months, he looked for acting opportunities while doing other jobs. He worked in Delmar Hotel, [Marine Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Drive,_Mumbai "Marine Drive, Mumbai") for eight months, after which he got a chance to act in 1948.

Because of help from writer [Saadat Hasan Manto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saadat_Hasan_Manto "Saadat Hasan Manto") and actor [Shyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shyam_(actor) "Shyam (actor)"), he got a role in the [Bombay Talkies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_Talkies "Bombay Talkies")' film, _[Ziddi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziddi\_(1948\_film) "Ziddi (1948 film)")_ which starred [Dev Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand") and [Kamini Kaushal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal "Kamini Kaushal") and was directed by [Shaheed Latif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed_Latif "Shaheed Latif"). The movie launched Pran's career in Bombay. Incidentally, it proved to be Dev Anand's big break as a hero.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-bol-9)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-16) By 1950 he had been gradually established as a premier villain in Hindi cinema. Within a week of _Ziddi_'s success, he had signed three more films – S M Yusuf's _Grihasti_ (1948), which became a diamond jubilee hit, [Prabhat Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prabhat_Film_Company "Prabhat Film Company")'s _Apradhi_ (1949) and Wali Mohammad's _Putli_ (1949). By then, Wali Mohammad, who was responsible for Pran's first role, had come to Bombay and became a producer, setting up an office at Famous Studios, near [Mahalaxmi Racecourse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahalaxmi_Racecourse "Mahalaxmi Racecourse").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-kis-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-18) In the 1940s, romantic duets featuring him, like the songs "Tere Naaz Uthane Ko Jee Chahta Hai" from _Grihasti_, opposite Shardha, and from _Khandaan_ (1942), with Noor Jehan, became popular in the 1940s. The way he expressed his dialogues in films such as _Sheesh Mahal_ (1950), a series of disguises he made in _Adalat_ (1958), and the rapport he shared with vamps like [Kuldip Kaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuldip_Kaur "Kuldip Kaur") in _Jashan_ (1955) showcased his versatility in the 1950s.

As a villain, Pran's initial successful films were _Ziddi_ and _Bari Behan_ (1949). Pran's trademark blowing of smoke rings first appeared in the latter film.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-19) He was regularly offered the role of the main villain or of a negative character in films with [Dilip Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar"), [Dev Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand") and [Raj Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Kapoor "Raj Kapoor") as the lead hero in the 1950s and 60s. From the 1950s directors like [M. V. Raman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._V._Raman "M. V. Raman"), [Nanabhai Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanabhai_Bhatt "Nanabhai Bhatt"), Kalidas, Ravindra Dave, [I. S. Johar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I._S._Johar "I. S. Johar") and [Bimal Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bimal_Roy "Bimal Roy") repeatedly cast him. Similarly in the 1960s, he was frequently in the directorial ventures of A. Bhim Singh, [Shakti Samanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Samanta "Shakti Samanta"), [Bhappi Sonie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhappi_Sonie "Bhappi Sonie"), [K. Amarnath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Amarnath "K. Amarnath"), [Nasir Hussain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasir_Hussain "Nasir Hussain") and others. In the 1970s, newer, younger directors and producers cast him in their films even though Pran asked for the highest price among supporting actors from 1968 to 1982.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-20)

Pran's performance as the negative character was appreciated especially in Dilip Kumar starrers such as _[Azaad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azaad\_(1955\_film) "Azaad (1955 film)")_ (1955), _[Devdas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devdas\_(1955\_film) "Devdas (1955 film)")_ (1955), _[Madhumati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhumati "Madhumati")_ (1958), _[Dil Diya Dard Liya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Diya\_Dard\_Liya "Dil Diya Dard Liya")_ (1966), _[Ram Aur Shyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram\_Aur\_Shyam "Ram Aur Shyam")_ (1967) and _[Aadmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aadmi\_(1968\_film) "Aadmi (1968 film)")_ (1968); and films with Dev Anand as the lead man such as _[Ziddi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziddi\_(1948\_film) "Ziddi (1948 film)")_ (1948), _[Munimji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munimji "Munimji")_ (1955), _[Amar Deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar\_Deep\_(1958\_film) "Amar Deep (1958 film)")_ (1958), _[Jab Pyar Kisi Se Hota Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jab\_Pyar\_Kisi\_Se\_Hota\_Hai "Jab Pyar Kisi Se Hota Hai")_ (1961); and with Raj Kapoor in _[Aah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aah\_(film) "Aah (film)")_ (1953), _[Chori Chori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chori\_Chori\_(1956\_film) "Chori Chori (1956 film)")_ (1956), _[Jagte Raho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagte\_Raho "Jagte Raho")_ (1956), _[Chhalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chhalia "Chhalia")_ (1960), _[Jis Desh Mein Ganga Behti Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jis\_Desh\_Mein\_Ganga\_Behti\_Hai "Jis Desh Mein Ganga Behti Hai")_ (1960) and _Dil Hi Toh Hai_ (1963). Films with him as the lead hero, _Pilpili Saheb_ (1954) and then _Halaku_ in 1956, were big hits too. He had roles in several genres, like as a pirate in _Sindbad the Sailor_ (1952) and _Daughter of Sindbad_ (1958); in action-packed thrillers like _Azad_ (1955); historicals like _Aan_ (1952) and _Raj Tilak_ (1958); social themes like _Baradari_ (1955); and light romances like _Munimji_ (1955) and _Asha_ (1957).[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-21) In the 1960s and early 1970s, despite being in his 40s, he continued to play pivotal roles as a character in the age range of 25 to 30 in films with [Shammi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammi_Kapoor "Shammi Kapoor"), [Joy Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_Mukherjee "Joy Mukherjee"), [Rajendra Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajendra_Kumar "Rajendra Kumar") and [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra") as the lead heroes.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-22) From the early 1950s to the early 1970s, Pran gained particular notoriety due to his frequent roles as a villain.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Akhtar-23) From 1964, with _[Pooja Ke Phool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pooja\_Ke\_Phool "Pooja Ke Phool")_ and _[Kashmir Ki Kali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmir\_Ki\_Kali "Kashmir Ki Kali")_, he also brought a comical side to his negative characters. While Dilip Kumar and Raj Kapoor's careers as the young hero started to decline in the late 1960s and Rajendra Kumar and Shammi Kapoor stopped playing the lead by 1973, Pran continued with his roles. His association with Dev Anand, begun in 1948, continued even during the 1970s and the 1980s with _[Johny Mera Naam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johny\_Mera\_Naam "Johny Mera Naam")_ (1970), _[Yeh Gulistan Hamara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeh\_Gulistan\_Hamara "Yeh Gulistan Hamara")_ (1972), _[Joshila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshila "Joshila")_ (1973), _[Warrant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warrant\_(1975\_film) "Warrant (1975 film)")_ (1975) and _[Des Pardes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Des\_Pardes\_(1978\_film) "Des Pardes (1978 film)")_ (1978).

Pran played roles in comedy films starring [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar") and [Mehmood Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mehmood_Ali "Mehmood Ali") in the lead. His collaborations with Mehmood include _[Sadhu Aur Shaitaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadhu\_Aur\_Shaitaan "Sadhu Aur Shaitaan")_ (1968), _Lakhon Me Ek_ (1971) and with Kishore Kumar include _Chham Chhama Chham_ (1952), _[Aasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aasha\_(1957\_film) "Aasha (1957 film)")_ (1957), _[Bewaqoof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bewaqoof "Bewaqoof")_ (1960), _[Half Ticket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half\_Ticket\_(1962\_film) "Half Ticket (1962 film)")_ (1962) and _Man-Mauji_ (1962).

### Later career (1967−retirement)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Later career (1967−retirement)")]

In the late 1960s, Pran played Malang Chacha, a veteran war hero, in [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar")'s film _[Upkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upkar "Upkar")_ (1967). The [Kalyanji Anandji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalyanji_Anandji "Kalyanji Anandji") song "Kasme Waade Pyaar Wafaa" was picturised on him. In this film, Pran played a more sympathetic role. He received his first [Filmfare Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award "Filmfare Award") for _Upkar_. Kumar continued to cast him in pivotal roles in films such as _[Purab Aur Paschim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purab\_Aur\_Paschim "Purab Aur Paschim")_ (1970), _[Be-Imaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Be-Imaan "Be-Imaan")_ (1972), _[Sanyasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanyasi\_(1975\_film) "Sanyasi (1975 film)")_ (1975) and _[Dus Numbri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dus\_Numbri "Dus Numbri")_ (1976).

From 1967 onward he also acted in Bengali films, beginning with Ashim Banerjee's _Sonai Dighe_, where [Joy Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_Mukherjee "Joy Mukherjee") was the hero.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Ninety-24)

Pran played the supporting role in several of these, which replaced his image as the villain with that of a character actor. After 1969, he was offered the lead role in films like _Nanha Farishta_ (1969), _[Jangal Mein Mangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jangal\_Mein\_Mangal "Jangal Mein Mangal")_ (1972), _Dharma_ (1973), _[Ek Kunwari Ek Kunwara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ek\_Kunwari\_Ek\_Kunwara "Ek Kunwari Ek Kunwara")_ (1973) and _[Rahu Ketu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahu\_Ketu\_(1978\_film) "Rahu Ketu (1978 film)")_ (1978).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-HT_Life_of_Pran-25)

Pran and [Ashok Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashok_Kumar "Ashok Kumar") were very close friends in professional and real life. They acted in 27 films together from 1951 to 1987 starting with _Afsana_ (1951). Their other films include _Mr. X_ (1957), _[Adhikar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adhikar\_(1971\_film) "Adhikar (1971 film)")_ (1971), _[Victoria No. 203](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria\_No.\_203\_(1972\_film) "Victoria No. 203 (1972 film)")_ (1972), _[Chori Mera Kaam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chori\_Mera\_Kaam "Chori Mera Kaam")_ (1975) and _Raja Aur Rana_ (1984). Sung by [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar"), the songs "Hum Bolega To Bologe Ke Bolta Hai" from _[Kasauti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasauti "Kasauti")_ (1974) and "Micheal Daru Peeke Dandha Kartha Hai" from _[Majboor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majboor\_(1974\_film) "Majboor (1974 film)")_ (1974), picturised on Pran, were very popular.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

From 1969 to 1982, Pran was one of the highest-paid actors in Bollywood.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-26) He played the lead role in the film _[Aurat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurat\_(1967\_film) "Aurat (1967 film)")_ (1967) paired opposite [Padmini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmini_(actress) "Padmini (actress)"), with [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") in a supporting role. Pran and Khanna worked in five more films — _[Maryada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryada\_(1971\_film) "Maryada (1971 film)")_ (1971), _[Jaanwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaanwar\_(1983\_film) "Jaanwar (1983 film)")_ (1983), _[Souten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Souten "Souten")_ (1983), _[Bewafai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bewafai "Bewafai")_ (1985) and _[Durgaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durgaa "Durgaa")_ (1985). In 1973, he recommended [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") to [Prakash Mehra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prakash_Mehra "Prakash Mehra") for the character of Vijay in _Zanjeer_, a role earlier offered to Dev Anand and Dharmendra. Pran's role as Sher Khan, with his red wig and beard and [Pathan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathan "Pathan") I style was well appreciated.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-27) Pran acted with Bachchan in about 14 films with notable ones being _[Zanjeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zanjeer\_(1973\_film) "Zanjeer (1973 film)")_ (1973), _[Majboor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majboor\_(1974\_film) "Majboor (1974 film)")_ (1974), _[Don](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don\_(1978\_film) "Don (1978 film)")_ (1978), _[Amar Akbar Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar\_Akbar\_Anthony\_(1977\_film) "Amar Akbar Anthony (1977 film)")_ (1977), _[Dostana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dostana\_(1980\_film) "Dostana (1980 film)")_ (1980), _[Kaalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaalia "Kaalia")_ (1981), _[Naseeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeb\_(1981\_film) "Naseeb (1981 film)")_ (1981) and _[Sharaabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharaabi "Sharaabi")_ (1984).

Pran occasionally accepted antagonistic roles from 1971 to 1992. He appeared as a villain in films like _[Maryada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryada\_(1971\_film) "Maryada (1971 film)")_, _Naya Zamana_, _Jawan Muhabat_, _Aan Baan_, _Roop Tera Mastana_, _Yeh Gulistan Hamara_, _Gaddar_, _Rahu Ketu_, _Andha Kanoon_ (1983), _Duniya_ (1984), _Insaaf Kaun Karega_, _Durgaa_, _Bewafai_, _Hoshiyar_, _Dharm Adhikari_ and _Azaad Desh Ke Ghulam_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-HT_Life_of_Pran-25) Pran had dual roles in _Khoon Ka Rishta_, _Insaaf_ and _Jangal Mein Mangal_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-28)

He produced the movie _[Lakshmanrekha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakshmanrekha "Lakshmanrekha")_ in 1991, the only one he produced in his Bollywood career, and played Kishan Lal Sharma in the movie.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-facts-29)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Pran_90th_bday.jpg/250px-Pran_90th_bday.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pran_90th_bday.jpg)

Pran at his 90th birthday in 2010.

In 1998, at the age of 78, Pran suffered a heart attack,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-30) after which he started rejecting film offers due to age-related problems. But in the 1990s, Amitabh Bachchan requested Pran to do roles in his home productions _[Tere Mere Sapne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tere\_Mere\_Sapne\_(1996\_film) "Tere Mere Sapne (1996 film)")_ (1996) and _[Mrityudata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrityudata "Mrityudata")_ (1997). Pran made an exception by acting in them to help Bachchan through a difficult time in his career. In 1997, his character in _Mrityudaata_ was modified to compensate for Pran's shaking legs in real life and in _Tere Mere Sapne_, his shots were taken with him seated. After 2000, he made a few guest appearances.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Ninety-24)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Pran married Shukla Sikand (née Ahluwalia; 1 October 1924 – 26 March 2016) on 18 April 1945 and has two sons, Arvind (born 11 August 1946) and [Sunil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunil_Sikand "Sunil Sikand") (born 19 September 1949), and a daughter Pinky (born 1953).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-of-7)

## Illness and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Illness and death")]

He was treated at the [Lilavati Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilavati_Hospital_and_Research_Centre "Lilavati Hospital and Research Centre") and died on 12 July 2013 at the age of 93. He had been admitted to hospital a few times in the last few months for deteriorating health; at some point he was battling pneumonia.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-31) Pran's death was widely noted by statesmen and his fellow entertainers.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-32) Prime Minister [Manmohan Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manmohan_Singh "Manmohan Singh") paid his condolences on his death and called him "an icon".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-33) Veteran actor [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") tweeted his feelings about his death calling him a "magnificent pillar" of the film industry.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Mourn-34)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Pran had a six-decade career in [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema") and is one of the most celebrated actors in the industry. His acting is said to have been effective enough to desist people from naming their children "Pran" because of his negative roles,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Akhtar-23) while the industry had started calling him "Pran Sahab".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-35) His favourite line "Barkhurdaar" became immensely popular. In fact he was paid more than most male leads of his time, often most people would go to watch movies to only watch Pran.

In 2000, Bunny Reuben, a film journalist, authored a biography on Pran, titled "...and Pran". The name of this book arises from the fact that in the majority of Pran's movies, his name was credited in the last after all the other actors, "....and Pran". His biography, "...and Pran", was a tribute to about 250 of his 350 movies that had his name at the end of the credits, usually with the words "...and Pran" and sometimes "...above all, Pran".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-36) In 2012, he gave his handprint for "Legend's Walk", a waterfront promenade in [Bandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandra "Bandra").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-37) In 2022, Pran was placed in _[Outlook India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlook\_India "Outlook India")_'s "75 Best Bollywood Actors" list.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-38)

## Awards and honours

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Awards and honours")]

Pran has been honoured with awards for his portrayal of negative characters. He has received three [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards") in the [Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Best_Supporting_Actor_Award "Filmfare Best Supporting Actor Award") category for _Upkar_, _Aansoo Ban Gaye Phool_ and _Be-Imaan_. However, in 1973 when he was awarded for his role of constable Ram Singh in _Be-Imaan_, he refused to accept the award stating that the [Filmfare Award for Best Music Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Music_Director "Filmfare Award for Best Music Director") should have gone to [Ghulam Mohammed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghulam_Mohammed_(composer) "Ghulam Mohammed (composer)") for _[Pakeezah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakeezah "Pakeezah")_ and not to the musical duo [Shankar Jaikishan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar_Jaikishan "Shankar Jaikishan") for _Be-imaan_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-PranWebsite_awards-40) He was awarded three [Bengal Film Journalists' Association Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Film_Journalists'_Association_Awards "Bengal Film Journalists' Association Awards") for his supporting roles.

For his vast contributions to Indian cinema, Pran has been honoured with Lifetime Achievement awards, including those of Filmfare, [Star Screen Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Screen_Awards "Star Screen Awards") and [Zee Cine Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zee_Cine_Awards "Zee Cine Awards"). In 2001, the [Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") conferred the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") on him. In April 2013, he was announced to be the winner of the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award"), the most prestigious award of Indian cinema, presented by the Government of India. The award was presented to him at the [60th National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/60th_National_Film_Awards "60th National Film Awards") for his lifetime of work in the film industry.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-41) He could not attend the [60th National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/60th_National_Film_Awards "60th National Film Awards") in May 2013 where he was to be presented the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award"). Instead, Information and Broadcasting minister [Manish Tewari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manish_Tewari "Manish Tewari") presented the award at Pran's home in Mumbai. Celebrities congratulated him on this occasion with [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") calling him "a large pillar of the Indian Film Industry" on [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-42) He was a contender of the award for the previous year with [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar") and [Vyjayanthimala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyjayanthimala "Vyjayanthimala"), but [Soumitra Chatterjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soumitra_Chatterjee "Soumitra Chatterjee") was chosen as the awardee.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-43)

**Pran Krishan Sikand** (pronounced[[pra:n]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu"); 12 February 1920 – 12 July 2013), better known [mononymously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mononymous_person "Mononymous person") as **Pran**, was an Indian actor who worked in [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema"). He was one of the most successful and respected actors in the history of [Indian cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cinema "Indian cinema"); in a career spanning over six decades he was also one of the highest-paid actors of his time.

Pran was in/famous for his [villain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villain "Villain") roles, and a highly regarded character actor in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") from the 1940s to the 1990s.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-1) He played heroes from 1940 to 1947, negative roles from 1942 to 1991, and supporting and character roles from 1967 to 2007. From the late 1940s through the 70s was the peak of Pran's career as a villain, especially in the 1950s and 60s: his interpretations were the first true personification of "evil" on the Indian screen, and the intensity of his portrayals of negative/villainous characters was such that the given name "Pran" fell into disuse.

In a long and prolific career, Pran appeared in over [362 films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_filmography "Pran filmography"). He played the leading man in _[Khandaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khandan\_(1942\_film) "Khandan (1942 film)")_ (1942), _Pilpili Saheb_ (1954) and _[Halaku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halaku\_(film) "Halaku (film)")_ (1956), and was known for his roles in _[Madhumati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhumati "Madhumati")_ (1958), _[Jis Desh Mein Ganga Behti Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jis\_Desh\_Mein\_Ganga\_Behti\_Hai "Jis Desh Mein Ganga Behti Hai")_ (1960), _[Shaheed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed\_(1965\_film) "Shaheed (1965 film)")_ (1965), _[Upkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upkar "Upkar")_ (1967), _[Ram Aur Shyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram\_Aur\_Shyam "Ram Aur Shyam")_ (1967), _[Aansoo Ban Gaye Phool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aansoo\_Ban\_Gaye\_Phool "Aansoo Ban Gaye Phool")_ (1969), _[Purab Aur Paschim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purab\_Aur\_Paschim "Purab Aur Paschim")_ (1970), _[Johny Mera Naam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johny\_Mera\_Naam "Johny Mera Naam")_ (1970), _[Victoria No. 203](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria\_No.\_203\_(1972\_film) "Victoria No. 203 (1972 film)")_ (1972), _[Be-Imaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Be-Imaan "Be-Imaan")_ (1972), _[Zanjeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zanjeer\_(1973\_film) "Zanjeer (1973 film)")_ (1973), _[Majboor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majboor\_(1974\_film) "Majboor (1974 film)")_ (1974), _[Amar Akbar Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar\_Akbar\_Anthony "Amar Akbar Anthony")_ (1977), _[Don](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don\_(1978\_film) "Don (1978 film)")_ (1978), _[Sharaabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharaabi "Sharaabi")_ (1984) and _[Duniya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duniya\_(1984\_film) "Duniya (1984 film)")_ (1984).

Pran received many [#Awards and honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#Awards_and_honours) in his career, including the [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor") in 1967, 1969 and 1972, and was awarded the [Filmfare Special Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Special_Award "Filmfare Special Award") in 1997. He was named _"Villain of the Millennium"_ by [Stardust Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stardust_Awards "Stardust Awards") in 2000.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-2) The [Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") honoured him with the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") Award in 2001[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Padma_Awards-3) for his contributions to [the arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_arts "The arts"). He was honoured in 2013 with the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award"), the highest national award for cinema artists, by the Government of India. In 2010, he was named on the list of CNN's Top 25 Asian actors of all time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-5)

Pran died on 12 July 2013 at the age of 93 at Mumbai's [Lilavati Hospital and Research Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilavati_Hospital_and_Research_Centre "Lilavati Hospital and Research Centre") after suffering a prolonged illness.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-6)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Pran was born on 12 February 1920 in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-of-7) into a wealthy [Punjabi Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_Hindu "Punjabi Hindu") family but raised in Ballimaran of [Old Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Delhi "Old Delhi") in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"). His father, Lala Kewal Krishan Sikand,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-8) was a [civil engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_engineer "Civil engineer") and a government civil contractor; his mother was Rameshwari. Pran was one of seven children; four sons and three daughters.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-bol-9)

Pran was academically gifted, especially in mathematics. His father had a transferable job, and so Pran studied in various places, including [Dehradun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehradun "Dehradun"), Lahore, [Kapurthala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapurthala "Kapurthala"), [Meerut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meerut "Meerut") and [Unnao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unnao "Unnao") (Uttar Pradesh), finally completing his [matriculation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matriculation "Matriculation") from Hamid School, in [Rampur (U.P.)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rampur,_Uttar_Pradesh "Rampur, Uttar Pradesh"). After that, he joined A. Das & Co., [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi") as an apprentice to become a professional photographer. He travelled to [Shimla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimla "Shimla") and played [Sita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sita "Sita") in a local staging of "[Ramlila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramlila "Ramlila")". [Madan Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madan_Puri "Madan Puri") enacted the role of [Rama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rama "Rama") in this play.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-10)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career (1940–1967)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career (1940–1967)")]

Pran got his first role in [Dalsukh M. Pancholi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalsukh_M._Pancholi "Dalsukh M. Pancholi")'s [Punjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_language "Punjabi language") film _[Yamla Jat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamla\_Jat "Yamla Jat")_ (1940) because of an accidental meeting with writer Wali Mohammad Wali at a shop in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-11) Directed by Moti B. Gidwani, the film featured [Noor Jehan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noor_Jehan "Noor Jehan") and [Durga Khote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durga_Khote "Durga Khote"). This was followed by small roles in the film _Chaudhary_ and _Khajanchi_, both in 1941. Pancholi cast him again in _[Khandaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khandaan\_(1942\_film) "Khandaan (1942 film)")_ (1942), which was Pran's first [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi")-language film. It featured him as a [romantic hero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_hero "Romantic hero"), opposite Noor Jehan, who had acted with him in _Yamla Jat_ as a child artist.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-tri-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-14) In _Khandaan_, she was under 15 years old and compensated for the difference in their heights in [close-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close-up "Close-up") shots by standing on top of bricks.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-15) In the [pre-independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India") era, director Gidwani cast Pran in more films like _Kaise Kahoon_ (1945) and _Khamosh Nigahen_ (1946).

Pran had acted in 22 films from 1942 to 1946 in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore"); 18 were released by 1947. Due to [India's partition in 1947](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India"), his career had a brief break. His films from 1944 to 1947 were made in undivided India, but _Taraash_ (1951) and _Khanabadosh_ (1952) (both co-starring [Manorama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manorama_(Hindi_actress) "Manorama (Hindi actress)")) were released only in Pakistan after Partition. He left Lahore and arrived in [Bombay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay "Bombay"). For a few months, he looked for acting opportunities while doing other jobs. He worked in Delmar Hotel, [Marine Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Drive,_Mumbai "Marine Drive, Mumbai") for eight months, after which he got a chance to act in 1948.

Because of help from writer [Saadat Hasan Manto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saadat_Hasan_Manto "Saadat Hasan Manto") and actor [Shyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shyam_(actor) "Shyam (actor)"), he got a role in the [Bombay Talkies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_Talkies "Bombay Talkies")' film, _[Ziddi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziddi\_(1948\_film) "Ziddi (1948 film)")_ which starred [Dev Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand") and [Kamini Kaushal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal "Kamini Kaushal") and was directed by [Shaheed Latif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed_Latif "Shaheed Latif"). The movie launched Pran's career in Bombay. Incidentally, it proved to be Dev Anand's big break as a hero.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-bol-9)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-16) By 1950 he had been gradually established as a premier villain in Hindi cinema. Within a week of _Ziddi_'s success, he had signed three more films – S M Yusuf's _Grihasti_ (1948), which became a diamond jubilee hit, [Prabhat Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prabhat_Film_Company "Prabhat Film Company")'s _Apradhi_ (1949) and Wali Mohammad's _Putli_ (1949). By then, Wali Mohammad, who was responsible for Pran's first role, had come to Bombay and became a producer, setting up an office at Famous Studios, near [Mahalaxmi Racecourse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahalaxmi_Racecourse "Mahalaxmi Racecourse").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-kis-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-18) In the 1940s, romantic duets featuring him, like the songs "Tere Naaz Uthane Ko Jee Chahta Hai" from _Grihasti_, opposite Shardha, and from _Khandaan_ (1942), with Noor Jehan, became popular in the 1940s. The way he expressed his dialogues in films such as _Sheesh Mahal_ (1950), a series of disguises he made in _Adalat_ (1958), and the rapport he shared with vamps like [Kuldip Kaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuldip_Kaur "Kuldip Kaur") in _Jashan_ (1955) showcased his versatility in the 1950s.

As a villain, Pran's initial successful films were _Ziddi_ and _Bari Behan_ (1949). Pran's trademark blowing of smoke rings first appeared in the latter film.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-19) He was regularly offered the role of the main villain or of a negative character in films with [Dilip Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar"), [Dev Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand") and [Raj Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Kapoor "Raj Kapoor") as the lead hero in the 1950s and 60s. From the 1950s directors like [M. V. Raman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._V._Raman "M. V. Raman"), [Nanabhai Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanabhai_Bhatt "Nanabhai Bhatt"), Kalidas, Ravindra Dave, [I. S. Johar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I._S._Johar "I. S. Johar") and [Bimal Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bimal_Roy "Bimal Roy") repeatedly cast him. Similarly in the 1960s, he was frequently in the directorial ventures of A. Bhim Singh, [Shakti Samanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Samanta "Shakti Samanta"), [Bhappi Sonie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhappi_Sonie "Bhappi Sonie"), [K. Amarnath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Amarnath "K. Amarnath"), [Nasir Hussain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasir_Hussain "Nasir Hussain") and others. In the 1970s, newer, younger directors and producers cast him in their films even though Pran asked for the highest price among supporting actors from 1968 to 1982.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-20)

Pran's performance as the negative character was appreciated especially in Dilip Kumar starrers such as _[Azaad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azaad\_(1955\_film) "Azaad (1955 film)")_ (1955), _[Devdas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devdas\_(1955\_film) "Devdas (1955 film)")_ (1955), _[Madhumati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhumati "Madhumati")_ (1958), _[Dil Diya Dard Liya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Diya\_Dard\_Liya "Dil Diya Dard Liya")_ (1966), _[Ram Aur Shyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram\_Aur\_Shyam "Ram Aur Shyam")_ (1967) and _[Aadmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aadmi\_(1968\_film) "Aadmi (1968 film)")_ (1968); and films with Dev Anand as the lead man such as _[Ziddi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziddi\_(1948\_film) "Ziddi (1948 film)")_ (1948), _[Munimji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munimji "Munimji")_ (1955), _[Amar Deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar\_Deep\_(1958\_film) "Amar Deep (1958 film)")_ (1958), _[Jab Pyar Kisi Se Hota Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jab\_Pyar\_Kisi\_Se\_Hota\_Hai "Jab Pyar Kisi Se Hota Hai")_ (1961); and with Raj Kapoor in _[Aah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aah\_(film) "Aah (film)")_ (1953), _[Chori Chori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chori\_Chori\_(1956\_film) "Chori Chori (1956 film)")_ (1956), _[Jagte Raho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagte\_Raho "Jagte Raho")_ (1956), _[Chhalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chhalia "Chhalia")_ (1960), _[Jis Desh Mein Ganga Behti Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jis\_Desh\_Mein\_Ganga\_Behti\_Hai "Jis Desh Mein Ganga Behti Hai")_ (1960) and _Dil Hi Toh Hai_ (1963). Films with him as the lead hero, _Pilpili Saheb_ (1954) and then _Halaku_ in 1956, were big hits too. He had roles in several genres, like as a pirate in _Sindbad the Sailor_ (1952) and _Daughter of Sindbad_ (1958); in action-packed thrillers like _Azad_ (1955); historicals like _Aan_ (1952) and _Raj Tilak_ (1958); social themes like _Baradari_ (1955); and light romances like _Munimji_ (1955) and _Asha_ (1957).[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-21) In the 1960s and early 1970s, despite being in his 40s, he continued to play pivotal roles as a character in the age range of 25 to 30 in films with [Shammi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammi_Kapoor "Shammi Kapoor"), [Joy Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_Mukherjee "Joy Mukherjee"), [Rajendra Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajendra_Kumar "Rajendra Kumar") and [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra") as the lead heroes.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-22) From the early 1950s to the early 1970s, Pran gained particular notoriety due to his frequent roles as a villain.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Akhtar-23) From 1964, with _[Pooja Ke Phool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pooja\_Ke\_Phool "Pooja Ke Phool")_ and _[Kashmir Ki Kali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmir\_Ki\_Kali "Kashmir Ki Kali")_, he also brought a comical side to his negative characters. While Dilip Kumar and Raj Kapoor's careers as the young hero started to decline in the late 1960s and Rajendra Kumar and Shammi Kapoor stopped playing the lead by 1973, Pran continued with his roles. His association with Dev Anand, begun in 1948, continued even during the 1970s and the 1980s with _[Johny Mera Naam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johny\_Mera\_Naam "Johny Mera Naam")_ (1970), _[Yeh Gulistan Hamara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeh\_Gulistan\_Hamara "Yeh Gulistan Hamara")_ (1972), _[Joshila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshila "Joshila")_ (1973), _[Warrant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warrant\_(1975\_film) "Warrant (1975 film)")_ (1975) and _[Des Pardes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Des\_Pardes\_(1978\_film) "Des Pardes (1978 film)")_ (1978).

Pran played roles in comedy films starring [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar") and [Mehmood Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mehmood_Ali "Mehmood Ali") in the lead. His collaborations with Mehmood include _[Sadhu Aur Shaitaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadhu\_Aur\_Shaitaan "Sadhu Aur Shaitaan")_ (1968), _Lakhon Me Ek_ (1971) and with Kishore Kumar include _Chham Chhama Chham_ (1952), _[Aasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aasha\_(1957\_film) "Aasha (1957 film)")_ (1957), _[Bewaqoof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bewaqoof "Bewaqoof")_ (1960), _[Half Ticket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half\_Ticket\_(1962\_film) "Half Ticket (1962 film)")_ (1962) and _Man-Mauji_ (1962).

### Later career (1967−retirement)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Later career (1967−retirement)")]

In the late 1960s, Pran played Malang Chacha, a veteran war hero, in [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar")'s film _[Upkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upkar "Upkar")_ (1967). The [Kalyanji Anandji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalyanji_Anandji "Kalyanji Anandji") song "Kasme Waade Pyaar Wafaa" was picturised on him. In this film, Pran played a more sympathetic role. He received his first [Filmfare Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award "Filmfare Award") for _Upkar_. Kumar continued to cast him in pivotal roles in films such as _[Purab Aur Paschim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purab\_Aur\_Paschim "Purab Aur Paschim")_ (1970), _[Be-Imaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Be-Imaan "Be-Imaan")_ (1972), _[Sanyasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanyasi\_(1975\_film) "Sanyasi (1975 film)")_ (1975) and _[Dus Numbri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dus\_Numbri "Dus Numbri")_ (1976).

From 1967 onward he also acted in Bengali films, beginning with Ashim Banerjee's _Sonai Dighe_, where [Joy Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_Mukherjee "Joy Mukherjee") was the hero.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Ninety-24)

Pran played the supporting role in several of these, which replaced his image as the villain with that of a character actor. After 1969, he was offered the lead role in films like _Nanha Farishta_ (1969), _[Jangal Mein Mangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jangal\_Mein\_Mangal "Jangal Mein Mangal")_ (1972), _Dharma_ (1973), _[Ek Kunwari Ek Kunwara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ek\_Kunwari\_Ek\_Kunwara "Ek Kunwari Ek Kunwara")_ (1973) and _[Rahu Ketu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahu\_Ketu\_(1978\_film) "Rahu Ketu (1978 film)")_ (1978).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-HT_Life_of_Pran-25)

Pran and [Ashok Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashok_Kumar "Ashok Kumar") were very close friends in professional and real life. They acted in 27 films together from 1951 to 1987 starting with _Afsana_ (1951). Their other films include _Mr. X_ (1957), _[Adhikar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adhikar\_(1971\_film) "Adhikar (1971 film)")_ (1971), _[Victoria No. 203](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria\_No.\_203\_(1972\_film) "Victoria No. 203 (1972 film)")_ (1972), _[Chori Mera Kaam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chori\_Mera\_Kaam "Chori Mera Kaam")_ (1975) and _Raja Aur Rana_ (1984). Sung by [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar"), the songs "Hum Bolega To Bologe Ke Bolta Hai" from _[Kasauti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasauti "Kasauti")_ (1974) and "Micheal Daru Peeke Dandha Kartha Hai" from _[Majboor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majboor\_(1974\_film) "Majboor (1974 film)")_ (1974), picturised on Pran, were very popular.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

From 1969 to 1982, Pran was one of the highest-paid actors in Bollywood.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-26) He played the lead role in the film _[Aurat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurat\_(1967\_film) "Aurat (1967 film)")_ (1967) paired opposite [Padmini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmini_(actress) "Padmini (actress)"), with [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") in a supporting role. Pran and Khanna worked in five more films — _[Maryada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryada\_(1971\_film) "Maryada (1971 film)")_ (1971), _[Jaanwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaanwar\_(1983\_film) "Jaanwar (1983 film)")_ (1983), _[Souten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Souten "Souten")_ (1983), _[Bewafai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bewafai "Bewafai")_ (1985) and _[Durgaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durgaa "Durgaa")_ (1985). In 1973, he recommended [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") to [Prakash Mehra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prakash_Mehra "Prakash Mehra") for the character of Vijay in _Zanjeer_, a role earlier offered to Dev Anand and Dharmendra. Pran's role as Sher Khan, with his red wig and beard and [Pathan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathan "Pathan") I style was well appreciated.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-27) Pran acted with Bachchan in about 14 films with notable ones being _[Zanjeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zanjeer\_(1973\_film) "Zanjeer (1973 film)")_ (1973), _[Majboor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majboor\_(1974\_film) "Majboor (1974 film)")_ (1974), _[Don](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don\_(1978\_film) "Don (1978 film)")_ (1978), _[Amar Akbar Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar\_Akbar\_Anthony\_(1977\_film) "Amar Akbar Anthony (1977 film)")_ (1977), _[Dostana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dostana\_(1980\_film) "Dostana (1980 film)")_ (1980), _[Kaalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaalia "Kaalia")_ (1981), _[Naseeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeb\_(1981\_film) "Naseeb (1981 film)")_ (1981) and _[Sharaabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharaabi "Sharaabi")_ (1984).

Pran occasionally accepted antagonistic roles from 1971 to 1992. He appeared as a villain in films like _[Maryada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryada\_(1971\_film) "Maryada (1971 film)")_, _Naya Zamana_, _Jawan Muhabat_, _Aan Baan_, _Roop Tera Mastana_, _Yeh Gulistan Hamara_, _Gaddar_, _Rahu Ketu_, _Andha Kanoon_ (1983), _Duniya_ (1984), _Insaaf Kaun Karega_, _Durgaa_, _Bewafai_, _Hoshiyar_, _Dharm Adhikari_ and _Azaad Desh Ke Ghulam_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-HT_Life_of_Pran-25) Pran had dual roles in _Khoon Ka Rishta_, _Insaaf_ and _Jangal Mein Mangal_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-28)

He produced the movie _[Lakshmanrekha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakshmanrekha "Lakshmanrekha")_ in 1991, the only one he produced in his Bollywood career, and played Kishan Lal Sharma in the movie.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-facts-29)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Pran_90th_bday.jpg/250px-Pran_90th_bday.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pran_90th_bday.jpg)

Pran at his 90th birthday in 2010.

In 1998, at the age of 78, Pran suffered a heart attack,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-30) after which he started rejecting film offers due to age-related problems. But in the 1990s, Amitabh Bachchan requested Pran to do roles in his home productions _[Tere Mere Sapne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tere\_Mere\_Sapne\_(1996\_film) "Tere Mere Sapne (1996 film)")_ (1996) and _[Mrityudata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrityudata "Mrityudata")_ (1997). Pran made an exception by acting in them to help Bachchan through a difficult time in his career. In 1997, his character in _Mrityudaata_ was modified to compensate for Pran's shaking legs in real life and in _Tere Mere Sapne_, his shots were taken with him seated. After 2000, he made a few guest appearances.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Ninety-24)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Pran married Shukla Sikand (née Ahluwalia; 1 October 1924 – 26 March 2016) on 18 April 1945 and has two sons, Arvind (born 11 August 1946) and [Sunil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunil_Sikand "Sunil Sikand") (born 19 September 1949), and a daughter Pinky (born 1953).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-of-7)

## Illness and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Illness and death")]

He was treated at the [Lilavati Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilavati_Hospital_and_Research_Centre "Lilavati Hospital and Research Centre") and died on 12 July 2013 at the age of 93. He had been admitted to hospital a few times in the last few months for deteriorating health; at some point he was battling pneumonia.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-31) Pran's death was widely noted by statesmen and his fellow entertainers.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-32) Prime Minister [Manmohan Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manmohan_Singh "Manmohan Singh") paid his condolences on his death and called him "an icon".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-33) Veteran actor [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") tweeted his feelings about his death calling him a "magnificent pillar" of the film industry.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Mourn-34)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Pran had a six-decade career in [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema") and is one of the most celebrated actors in the industry. His acting is said to have been effective enough to desist people from naming their children "Pran" because of his negative roles,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-Akhtar-23) while the industry had started calling him "Pran Sahab".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-35) His favourite line "Barkhurdaar" became immensely popular. In fact he was paid more than most male leads of his time, often most people would go to watch movies to only watch Pran.

In 2000, Bunny Reuben, a film journalist, authored a biography on Pran, titled "...and Pran". The name of this book arises from the fact that in the majority of Pran's movies, his name was credited in the last after all the other actors, "....and Pran". His biography, "...and Pran", was a tribute to about 250 of his 350 movies that had his name at the end of the credits, usually with the words "...and Pran" and sometimes "...above all, Pran".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-36) In 2012, he gave his handprint for "Legend's Walk", a waterfront promenade in [Bandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandra "Bandra").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-37) In 2022, Pran was placed in _[Outlook India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlook\_India "Outlook India")_'s "75 Best Bollywood Actors" list.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-38)

## Awards and honours

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pran_(actor)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Awards and honours")]

Pran has been honoured with awards for his portrayal of negative characters. He has received three [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards") in the [Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Best_Supporting_Actor_Award "Filmfare Best Supporting Actor Award") category for _Upkar_, _Aansoo Ban Gaye Phool_ and _Be-Imaan_. However, in 1973 when he was awarded for his role of constable Ram Singh in _Be-Imaan_, he refused to accept the award stating that the [Filmfare Award for Best Music Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Music_Director "Filmfare Award for Best Music Director") should have gone to [Ghulam Mohammed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghulam_Mohammed_(composer) "Ghulam Mohammed (composer)") for _[Pakeezah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakeezah "Pakeezah")_ and not to the musical duo [Shankar Jaikishan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar_Jaikishan "Shankar Jaikishan") for _Be-imaan_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-PranWebsite_awards-40) He was awarded three [Bengal Film Journalists' Association Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Film_Journalists'_Association_Awards "Bengal Film Journalists' Association Awards") for his supporting roles.

For his vast contributions to Indian cinema, Pran has been honoured with Lifetime Achievement awards, including those of Filmfare, [Star Screen Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Screen_Awards "Star Screen Awards") and [Zee Cine Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zee_Cine_Awards "Zee Cine Awards"). In 2001, the [Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") conferred the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") on him. In April 2013, he was announced to be the winner of the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award"), the most prestigious award of Indian cinema, presented by the Government of India. The award was presented to him at the [60th National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/60th_National_Film_Awards "60th National Film Awards") for his lifetime of work in the film industry.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-41) He could not attend the [60th National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/60th_National_Film_Awards "60th National Film Awards") in May 2013 where he was to be presented the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award"). Instead, Information and Broadcasting minister [Manish Tewari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manish_Tewari "Manish Tewari") presented the award at Pran's home in Mumbai. Celebrities congratulated him on this occasion with [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") calling him "a large pillar of the Indian Film Industry" on [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-42) He was a contender of the award for the previous year with [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar") and [Vyjayanthimala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyjayanthimala "Vyjayanthimala"), but [Soumitra Chatterjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soumitra_Chatterjee "Soumitra Chatterjee") was chosen as the awardee.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pran_(actor)#cite_note-43)

**Palappurathu Keshavan Surendranatha Thilakan** (15 July 1935 – 24 September 2012), known mononymously as **Thilakan**, was an Indian film and stage actor who appeared in over 200 [Malayalam films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_films "Malayalam films").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-4) Spanning more than five decades, Thilakan’s acting career was marked by critical acclaim for his versatility and powerful screen presence. He won several major honours including the [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") (2009) from the Government of India, multiple [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") and numerous [Kerala State Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Awards "Kerala State Film Awards"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-5) becoming the most frequent winner of the [Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Award_for_Second_Best_Actor "Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor").

Thilakan was known for his elaborate method acting and realistic, spontaneous performances[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-6) and is widely regarded as one of the greatest actors in Indian cinema, whose style influenced generations of Malayalam actors and audience.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Thilakan was the second of the six children of P. T. S. Keshavan of the Palappurathu house (1904–1972) and Devayani Amma (1912–2010). Thilakan was born in [Ayroor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayroor "Ayroor"), in the present-day [Pathanamthitta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathanamthitta "Pathanamthitta") district of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"). He had his primary education from Asan Pallikoodam, [Manikkal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manikkal "Manikkal") and St. Louis Catholic School, Nalamvayal, M. T. Seminary School Kottayam and Sree Narayana College, [Kollam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam "Kollam").He served in military while Jawaharlal Nehru was the Prime minister before starting his acting career. Thilakan lived in Ayroor until he started acting in films for which he moved to [Trivandrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trivandrum "Trivandrum").

Thilakan started his full-time career in acting after leaving college in the year 1956. During this period he and several friends formed a drama troupe called the _Mundakayam Nataka Samithy_ in [Mundakayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundakayam "Mundakayam"), where his father was working as an estate supervisor. He worked with the [Kerala People's Arts Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_People's_Arts_Club "Kerala People's Arts Club") till 1966, followed by stints in [Kalidasa Kalakendram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalidasa_Kalakendram "Kalidasa Kalakendram"), Changanacherry Geetha, and [P. J. Antony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Antony "P. J. Antony")'s troupe. He also performed in several radio plays presented by [All India Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_India_Radio "All India Radio").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Thilakan began his career in cinema with a role in the [P. J. Antony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Antony "P. J. Antony")-directed Malayalam movie _[Periyar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periyar\_(1973\_film) "Periyar (1973 film)")_ (1973). He then worked in _Gandharvakshetram_ and _[Ulkadal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oolkatal "Oolkatal")_ (1979). His first role as a lead character was as Kallu Varkey, a drunkard in _[Kolangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolangal\_(1981\_film) "Kolangal (1981 film)")_ (1981). Thilakan was awarded his first [Kerala State Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Awards "Kerala State Film Awards") in 1982 for his role in _[Yavanika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yavanika "Yavanika")_. He also won Kerala State Award for supporting actor in _[Yathra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yathra "Yathra")_ which also starred [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty").

In 1988, he received the [National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor") for his performance in _[Rithubhedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rithubhedam "Rithubhedam"),_ and again in 1994. In 1998, he won State awards for _[Santhanagopalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santhanagopalam "Santhanagopalam")_ and _[Gamanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamanam\_(1994\_film) "Gamanam (1994 film)")_. He was strongly favored[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-rediff1-7) to get another [National Film Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor") for his performance in the movie _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)"),_ but the award was given to [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") over Thilakan amidst suspicions of strong lobbying, as Amitabh had announced his retirement earlier that year.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-rediff1-7) The film _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_ was a milestone in Thilakan's career; in this film, he portrayed a helpless policeman silently watching the fate of his son, played by [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal"), who was corrupted by society's influences. In 1989 he performed in [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") starrer _[Mrugya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrugaya\_(1989\_film) "Mrugaya (1989 film)")_, in which his role of a Reverend Father Panangodan was well appreciated by critics and won him many accolades. In the 1990s Thilakan was part of many [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") and [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal") evergreen hit films. In 1987, he was appreciated for his role in _[Thaniyavarthanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thaniyavarthanam "Thaniyavarthanam")_ where he portrayed a man who is the head of a family where his nephew played by Mammootty becomes lunatic due to superstition and lack of awareness of mental health. He was awarded the [Second Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Award_for_Second_Best_Actor "Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor") for _[Thaniyavarthanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thaniyavarthanam "Thaniyavarthanam")_. In the same year, he also played the comic role of _Ananthan Nambiar_ in the cult-classic comedy movie _[Nadodikkattu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadodikkattu "Nadodikkattu")_, from which several of Thilakan's lines became very popular. He also starred in the National award winning movie _[Mathilukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathilukal "Mathilukal")_, which was directed by [Adoor Gopalakrishnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adoor_Gopalakrishnan "Adoor Gopalakrishnan") in which he played the role of a warden of the jail who develops a rapport with the prisoner [Vaikom Muhammad Basheer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom_Muhammad_Basheer "Vaikom Muhammad Basheer") (Mammootty). In 1993, he continued his role as the father of Sethu Madhavan (Mohanlal) in the movie _[Chenkol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chenkol "Chenkol")_. Like its prequel _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_, this movie also fared well both commercially and critically. His role as a retired mathematics teacher and headmaster C.P Chacko alias Kaduva Chacko, father of Thomas Chacko alias Aadu Thoma (Mohanlal), in the 1995 blockbuster movie _[Spadikam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spadikam "Spadikam")_ was well appreciated by critics and audiences alike. In 1998, he played the role of Dileep's father in the superhit _[Meenathil Thalikettu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenathil\_Thalikettu "Meenathil Thalikettu")_, and in his subsequent release he donned the role of a villain in the Kunchako Boban starrer _[Mayilpeelikavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayilpeelikkavu "Mayilpeelikkavu")_. In the same year, he was also seen in _[Chinthavishtayaya Shyamala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinthavishtayaya\_Shyamala "Chinthavishtayaya Shyamala")_. Other notable films Thilakan has acted in include _[Yathra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yathra "Yathra")_, _[Mukthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukthi "Mukthi")_, _[Kauravar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kauravar "Kauravar")_, _[Moonnam Pakkam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonnam\_Pakkam "Moonnam Pakkam")_, _[Kilukkam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilukkam "Kilukkam")_, _[Namukku Parkkan Munthiri Thoppukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namukku\_Parkkan\_Munthiri\_Thoppukal "Namukku Parkkan Munthiri Thoppukal")_, _[Mookkilla Rajyathu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mookilla\_Rajyathu "Mookilla Rajyathu")_, _[Randam Bhavam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randam\_Bhavam "Randam Bhavam")_, _[Kaattu Kuthira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattukuthira "Kattukuthira")_ and _[Yavanika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yavanika "Yavanika")_.

He has also acted in other South Indian languages, such as [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_cinema "Tamil cinema"), [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") and [Kannada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannada "Kannada").

Thilakan has portrayed a range of characters; however, his most well-known role is that of the father of [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal"), portraying a father-son duo. Movies where he donned this role include _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_, _[Spadikam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphadikam "Sphadikam")_, _[Narasimham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narasimham\_(film) "Narasimham (film)")_, _[Evidam Swargamanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evidam\_Swargamanu "Evidam Swargamanu")_, _[Pavithram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavithram\_(1994\_film) "Pavithram (1994 film)")_ and _Chenkol_. He has also played father roles to other popular actors, including with [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") in _[Sangham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangham\_(1988\_film) "Sangham (1988 film)")_, _[The Truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Truth\_(1998\_film) "The Truth (1998 film)")_, _[Oliyampukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliyampukal "Oliyampukal")_, _[No. 1 Snehatheeram Bangalore North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No.\_1\_Snehatheeram\_Bangalore\_North "No. 1 Snehatheeram Bangalore North")_ and _[Pallavur Devanarayanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallavur\_Devanarayanan "Pallavur Devanarayanan")_, with [Jayaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayaram "Jayaram") in _[Veendum Chila Veettu Karyangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veendum\_Chila\_Veettukaryangal "Veendum Chila Veettukaryangal")_ and _[Sandesam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandhesam "Sandhesam")_, with [Kunchacko Boban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunchacko_Boban "Kunchacko Boban") in _[Aniyathi Pravu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aniyathi\_Pravu "Aniyathi Pravu")_, with [Dileep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dileep "Dileep") in _[Punjabi House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi\_House "Punjabi House")_ and _[Meenathil Thalikettu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenathil\_Thalikettu "Meenathil Thalikettu")_ and with [Prithviraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithviraj_Sukumaran "Prithviraj Sukumaran") in _[Sathyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sathyam\_(2004\_film) "Sathyam (2004 film)")_. He has also played a number of antagonists, such as in _[Randam Bhavam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randam\_Bhavam "Randam Bhavam")_, _Karma_ and _[Kaalal Pada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaalal\_Pada "Kaalal Pada")_. He has played comical roles in films like _[Nadodikkattu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadodikkattu "Nadodikkattu")_ and _[Pattanapravesham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattanapravesham "Pattanapravesham")_ (as a coward underworld don), _[Mookkilla Rajyathu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mookilla\_Rajyathu "Mookilla Rajyathu")_ (as a break-out from a mental hospital), _[Kuttettan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuttettan "Kuttettan")_ (as a pimp) and _[Naaduvazhikal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naduvazhikal "Naduvazhikal")_ (as a good-for-nothing, vain person). He is also remembered for the role of comic underworld don _Damodarjj_ in [Sanmanassullavarkku Samadhanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanmanassullavarkku_Samadhanam "Sanmanassullavarkku Samadhanam"). Thilakan played lead roles in _[Ekantham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eakantham "Eakantham")_, _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)")_, _[Santhanagopalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santhanagopalam "Santhanagopalam")_, _[Kaattukuthira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattukuthira "Kattukuthira")_, _[My Dear Muthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Dear\_Muthachan "My Dear Muthachan")_, _Mukhamudra_ (double role), etc.
