In 2006, he was seen in the Suresh Gopi-Shaji Kailas blockbuster, [Chinthamani Kolacase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinthamani_Kolacase "Chinthamani Kolacase"), where he played the father of the title character Chinthamani enacted by [Bhavana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhavana_(Malayalam_actress) "Bhavana (Malayalam actress)"). In 2007, he acted in _[Ekantham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eakantham "Eakantham")_, for which he received a special mention from the jury.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-8) In 2009, he was also seen in [Pazhassi Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Varma_Pazhassi_Raja_(film) "Kerala Varma Pazhassi Raja (film)"), and in the same year he played [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal")'s father one last time in the actor's 300th movie _[Evidam Swargamanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evidam\_Swargamanu "Evidam Swargamanu")_. In 2011, he played a significant role in the [Prithviraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithviraj_Sukumaran "Prithviraj Sukumaran") blockbuster _[Indian Rupee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian\_Rupee\_(film) "Indian Rupee (film)")_ directed by [Renjith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renjith "Renjith"). In 2012, he played the role of Kareem Bhai in _[Ustad Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ustad\_Hotel "Ustad Hotel")_ and as the grandfather of Faizy, acted by [Dulquer Salmaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulquer_Salmaan "Dulquer Salmaan").

## Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Controversies")]

### National Film Award

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: National Film Award")]

Thilakan, in an interview, claimed that the then jury chairman Ashok Kumar was keen on giving him the [1991 National Film Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_National_Film_Awards "39th National Film Awards") for [Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor") for _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)")_ but that a [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") leader wanted the award to be given to [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") to woo him back to their party.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-9)

### FEFKA

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: FEFKA")]

In February 2010, it was reported that the producer of the movie _[Christian Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian\_Brothers\_(film) "Christian Brothers (film)")_ excluded Thilakan from the film at the request of the [Film Employees Federation of Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_Employees_Federation_of_Kerala "Film Employees Federation of Kerala") (FEFKA), the predominant film technicians association. Thilakan had been earlier signed for a role in the film. The exclusion was reportedly due to Thilakan acting in a film by director [Vinayan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinayan "Vinayan"), who till recently headed the rival association MACTA. On 3 February 2010, Thilakan publicly protested against the unofficial ban enforced on him by FEFKA and blamed FEFKA for engineering the ban. The [Association of Malayalam Movie Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Malayalam_Movie_Artists "Association of Malayalam Movie Artists") (AMMA) issued a show cause notice to Thilakan for bringing the issue into the public domain. Thilakan accused AMMA, of which he too is a member.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-11) On 20 February 2010 the [CPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India "Communist Party of India")'s trade union wing, [AITUC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AITUC "AITUC"), came out openly in support of Thilakan, while a senior party leader and [Rajya Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajya_Sabha "Rajya Sabha") member [K. E. Ismail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._E._Ismail "K. E. Ismail") expressed reservations about political involvement in the issue.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-12)

Thilakan was originally cast to play a role in a UAE-Indian co-production film _[Dam 999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam\_999 "Dam 999")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-13) He was later replaced following a notice from FEFKA stating that the association would boycott the film if Thilakan were to act. Sohan, the director, was forced to seek a substitute for Thilakan when it "came to the point that shooting might be disrupted."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-14) Eventually, [Rajit Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajit_Kapur "Rajit Kapur") was cast instead of Thilakan.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-amma-15) Some reports contended that Association of Malayalam Movie Artists (AMMA) also had intervened in Thilakan's replacement.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-amma-15) In response, Thilakan and his supporters orchestrated a march near the shooting location of the film in [Alappuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alappuzha "Alappuzha").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-16)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

### Relationships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Relationships")]

Thilakan's first partner was actress Santha with whom he appeared in several productions. Thilakan and Santha have three sons, Shaji, [Shammi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammi_Thilakan "Shammi Thilakan")&[Shobhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shobi_Thilakan "Shobi Thilakan"). Later, he had a second partner, his co-artist Sarojam with whom he had a son, Shibu Thilakan, and two daughters Dr. Sonia Thilakan and Sophia Ajith.

His grandson Abhimanyu made his debut in [Marco (2024)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_(2024_film) "Marco (2024 film)") starring [Unni Mukundan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unni_Mukundan "Unni Mukundan").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-17)

### Views

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Views")]

Thilakan was an [atheist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheist "Atheist")[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-18) throughout his life, and was a supporter of [Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party "Communist Party"). He was a member of many drama troupes which actively promoted Communism in Kerala. When he died, his dead body was draped with [Communist flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_symbolism "Communist symbolism").

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Death")]

For a long time, Thilakan dealt with numerous health issues like [diabetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabetes "Diabetes"), [hypertension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypertension "Hypertension") and [heart disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_disease "Heart disease"). He was hospitalized multiple times due to these problems. Finally, he was admitted to [Jubilee Mission Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jubilee_Mission_Hospital "Jubilee Mission Hospital") in [Thrissur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrissur "Thrissur") on 1 August 2012 after he collapsed during the shooting of the film _[Scene Onnu Nammude Veedu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scene\_Onnu\_Nammude\_Veedu "Scene Onnu Nammude Veedu")_. He was then shifted to KIMS Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram, and was in critical condition after suffering two heart attacks. Besides having cardiac problems, Thilakan was suffering from pneumonia. He was put on a ventilator and died on 24 September 2012.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-19) He was cremated with full state honours.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-20)

**Palappurathu Keshavan Surendranatha Thilakan** (15 July 1935 – 24 September 2012), known mononymously as **Thilakan**, was an Indian film and stage actor who appeared in over 200 [Malayalam films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_films "Malayalam films").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-4) Spanning more than five decades, Thilakan’s acting career was marked by critical acclaim for his versatility and powerful screen presence. He won several major honours including the [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") (2009) from the Government of India, multiple [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") and numerous [Kerala State Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Awards "Kerala State Film Awards"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-5) becoming the most frequent winner of the [Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Award_for_Second_Best_Actor "Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor").

Thilakan was known for his elaborate method acting and realistic, spontaneous performances[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-6) and is widely regarded as one of the greatest actors in Indian cinema, whose style influenced generations of Malayalam actors and audience.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Thilakan was the second of the six children of P. T. S. Keshavan of the Palappurathu house (1904–1972) and Devayani Amma (1912–2010). Thilakan was born in [Ayroor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayroor "Ayroor"), in the present-day [Pathanamthitta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathanamthitta "Pathanamthitta") district of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"). He had his primary education from Asan Pallikoodam, [Manikkal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manikkal "Manikkal") and St. Louis Catholic School, Nalamvayal, M. T. Seminary School Kottayam and Sree Narayana College, [Kollam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam "Kollam").He served in military while Jawaharlal Nehru was the Prime minister before starting his acting career. Thilakan lived in Ayroor until he started acting in films for which he moved to [Trivandrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trivandrum "Trivandrum").

Thilakan started his full-time career in acting after leaving college in the year 1956. During this period he and several friends formed a drama troupe called the _Mundakayam Nataka Samithy_ in [Mundakayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundakayam "Mundakayam"), where his father was working as an estate supervisor. He worked with the [Kerala People's Arts Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_People's_Arts_Club "Kerala People's Arts Club") till 1966, followed by stints in [Kalidasa Kalakendram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalidasa_Kalakendram "Kalidasa Kalakendram"), Changanacherry Geetha, and [P. J. Antony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Antony "P. J. Antony")'s troupe. He also performed in several radio plays presented by [All India Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_India_Radio "All India Radio").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Thilakan began his career in cinema with a role in the [P. J. Antony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Antony "P. J. Antony")-directed Malayalam movie _[Periyar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periyar\_(1973\_film) "Periyar (1973 film)")_ (1973). He then worked in _Gandharvakshetram_ and _[Ulkadal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oolkatal "Oolkatal")_ (1979). His first role as a lead character was as Kallu Varkey, a drunkard in _[Kolangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolangal\_(1981\_film) "Kolangal (1981 film)")_ (1981). Thilakan was awarded his first [Kerala State Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Awards "Kerala State Film Awards") in 1982 for his role in _[Yavanika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yavanika "Yavanika")_. He also won Kerala State Award for supporting actor in _[Yathra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yathra "Yathra")_ which also starred [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty").

In 1988, he received the [National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor") for his performance in _[Rithubhedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rithubhedam "Rithubhedam"),_ and again in 1994. In 1998, he won State awards for _[Santhanagopalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santhanagopalam "Santhanagopalam")_ and _[Gamanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamanam\_(1994\_film) "Gamanam (1994 film)")_. He was strongly favored[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-rediff1-7) to get another [National Film Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor") for his performance in the movie _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)"),_ but the award was given to [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") over Thilakan amidst suspicions of strong lobbying, as Amitabh had announced his retirement earlier that year.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-rediff1-7) The film _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_ was a milestone in Thilakan's career; in this film, he portrayed a helpless policeman silently watching the fate of his son, played by [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal"), who was corrupted by society's influences. In 1989 he performed in [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") starrer _[Mrugya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrugaya\_(1989\_film) "Mrugaya (1989 film)")_, in which his role of a Reverend Father Panangodan was well appreciated by critics and won him many accolades. In the 1990s Thilakan was part of many [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") and [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal") evergreen hit films. In 1987, he was appreciated for his role in _[Thaniyavarthanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thaniyavarthanam "Thaniyavarthanam")_ where he portrayed a man who is the head of a family where his nephew played by Mammootty becomes lunatic due to superstition and lack of awareness of mental health. He was awarded the [Second Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Award_for_Second_Best_Actor "Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor") for _[Thaniyavarthanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thaniyavarthanam "Thaniyavarthanam")_. In the same year, he also played the comic role of _Ananthan Nambiar_ in the cult-classic comedy movie _[Nadodikkattu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadodikkattu "Nadodikkattu")_, from which several of Thilakan's lines became very popular. He also starred in the National award winning movie _[Mathilukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathilukal "Mathilukal")_, which was directed by [Adoor Gopalakrishnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adoor_Gopalakrishnan "Adoor Gopalakrishnan") in which he played the role of a warden of the jail who develops a rapport with the prisoner [Vaikom Muhammad Basheer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom_Muhammad_Basheer "Vaikom Muhammad Basheer") (Mammootty). In 1993, he continued his role as the father of Sethu Madhavan (Mohanlal) in the movie _[Chenkol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chenkol "Chenkol")_. Like its prequel _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_, this movie also fared well both commercially and critically. His role as a retired mathematics teacher and headmaster C.P Chacko alias Kaduva Chacko, father of Thomas Chacko alias Aadu Thoma (Mohanlal), in the 1995 blockbuster movie _[Spadikam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spadikam "Spadikam")_ was well appreciated by critics and audiences alike. In 1998, he played the role of Dileep's father in the superhit _[Meenathil Thalikettu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenathil\_Thalikettu "Meenathil Thalikettu")_, and in his subsequent release he donned the role of a villain in the Kunchako Boban starrer _[Mayilpeelikavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayilpeelikkavu "Mayilpeelikkavu")_. In the same year, he was also seen in _[Chinthavishtayaya Shyamala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinthavishtayaya\_Shyamala "Chinthavishtayaya Shyamala")_. Other notable films Thilakan has acted in include _[Yathra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yathra "Yathra")_, _[Mukthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukthi "Mukthi")_, _[Kauravar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kauravar "Kauravar")_, _[Moonnam Pakkam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonnam\_Pakkam "Moonnam Pakkam")_, _[Kilukkam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilukkam "Kilukkam")_, _[Namukku Parkkan Munthiri Thoppukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namukku\_Parkkan\_Munthiri\_Thoppukal "Namukku Parkkan Munthiri Thoppukal")_, _[Mookkilla Rajyathu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mookilla\_Rajyathu "Mookilla Rajyathu")_, _[Randam Bhavam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randam\_Bhavam "Randam Bhavam")_, _[Kaattu Kuthira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattukuthira "Kattukuthira")_ and _[Yavanika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yavanika "Yavanika")_.

He has also acted in other South Indian languages, such as [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_cinema "Tamil cinema"), [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") and [Kannada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannada "Kannada").

Thilakan has portrayed a range of characters; however, his most well-known role is that of the father of [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal"), portraying a father-son duo. Movies where he donned this role include _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_, _[Spadikam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphadikam "Sphadikam")_, _[Narasimham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narasimham\_(film) "Narasimham (film)")_, _[Evidam Swargamanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evidam\_Swargamanu "Evidam Swargamanu")_, _[Pavithram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavithram\_(1994\_film) "Pavithram (1994 film)")_ and _Chenkol_. He has also played father roles to other popular actors, including with [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") in _[Sangham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangham\_(1988\_film) "Sangham (1988 film)")_, _[The Truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Truth\_(1998\_film) "The Truth (1998 film)")_, _[Oliyampukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliyampukal "Oliyampukal")_, _[No. 1 Snehatheeram Bangalore North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No.\_1\_Snehatheeram\_Bangalore\_North "No. 1 Snehatheeram Bangalore North")_ and _[Pallavur Devanarayanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallavur\_Devanarayanan "Pallavur Devanarayanan")_, with [Jayaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayaram "Jayaram") in _[Veendum Chila Veettu Karyangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veendum\_Chila\_Veettukaryangal "Veendum Chila Veettukaryangal")_ and _[Sandesam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandhesam "Sandhesam")_, with [Kunchacko Boban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunchacko_Boban "Kunchacko Boban") in _[Aniyathi Pravu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aniyathi\_Pravu "Aniyathi Pravu")_, with [Dileep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dileep "Dileep") in _[Punjabi House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi\_House "Punjabi House")_ and _[Meenathil Thalikettu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenathil\_Thalikettu "Meenathil Thalikettu")_ and with [Prithviraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithviraj_Sukumaran "Prithviraj Sukumaran") in _[Sathyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sathyam\_(2004\_film) "Sathyam (2004 film)")_. He has also played a number of antagonists, such as in _[Randam Bhavam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randam\_Bhavam "Randam Bhavam")_, _Karma_ and _[Kaalal Pada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaalal\_Pada "Kaalal Pada")_. He has played comical roles in films like _[Nadodikkattu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadodikkattu "Nadodikkattu")_ and _[Pattanapravesham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattanapravesham "Pattanapravesham")_ (as a coward underworld don), _[Mookkilla Rajyathu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mookilla\_Rajyathu "Mookilla Rajyathu")_ (as a break-out from a mental hospital), _[Kuttettan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuttettan "Kuttettan")_ (as a pimp) and _[Naaduvazhikal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naduvazhikal "Naduvazhikal")_ (as a good-for-nothing, vain person). He is also remembered for the role of comic underworld don _Damodarjj_ in [Sanmanassullavarkku Samadhanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanmanassullavarkku_Samadhanam "Sanmanassullavarkku Samadhanam"). Thilakan played lead roles in _[Ekantham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eakantham "Eakantham")_, _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)")_, _[Santhanagopalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santhanagopalam "Santhanagopalam")_, _[Kaattukuthira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattukuthira "Kattukuthira")_, _[My Dear Muthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Dear\_Muthachan "My Dear Muthachan")_, _Mukhamudra_ (double role), etc.

## Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Controversies")]

### National Film Award

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: National Film Award")]

Thilakan, in an interview, claimed that the then jury chairman Ashok Kumar was keen on giving him the [1991 National Film Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_National_Film_Awards "39th National Film Awards") for [Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor") for _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)")_ but that a [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") leader wanted the award to be given to [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") to woo him back to their party.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-9)

### FEFKA

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: FEFKA")]

In February 2010, it was reported that the producer of the movie _[Christian Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian\_Brothers\_(film) "Christian Brothers (film)")_ excluded Thilakan from the film at the request of the [Film Employees Federation of Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_Employees_Federation_of_Kerala "Film Employees Federation of Kerala") (FEFKA), the predominant film technicians association. Thilakan had been earlier signed for a role in the film. The exclusion was reportedly due to Thilakan acting in a film by director [Vinayan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinayan "Vinayan"), who till recently headed the rival association MACTA. On 3 February 2010, Thilakan publicly protested against the unofficial ban enforced on him by FEFKA and blamed FEFKA for engineering the ban. The [Association of Malayalam Movie Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Malayalam_Movie_Artists "Association of Malayalam Movie Artists") (AMMA) issued a show cause notice to Thilakan for bringing the issue into the public domain. Thilakan accused AMMA, of which he too is a member.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-11) On 20 February 2010 the [CPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India "Communist Party of India")'s trade union wing, [AITUC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AITUC "AITUC"), came out openly in support of Thilakan, while a senior party leader and [Rajya Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajya_Sabha "Rajya Sabha") member [K. E. Ismail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._E._Ismail "K. E. Ismail") expressed reservations about political involvement in the issue.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-12)

Thilakan was originally cast to play a role in a UAE-Indian co-production film _[Dam 999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam\_999 "Dam 999")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-13) He was later replaced following a notice from FEFKA stating that the association would boycott the film if Thilakan were to act. Sohan, the director, was forced to seek a substitute for Thilakan when it "came to the point that shooting might be disrupted."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-14) Eventually, [Rajit Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajit_Kapur "Rajit Kapur") was cast instead of Thilakan.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-amma-15) Some reports contended that Association of Malayalam Movie Artists (AMMA) also had intervened in Thilakan's replacement.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-amma-15) In response, Thilakan and his supporters orchestrated a march near the shooting location of the film in [Alappuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alappuzha "Alappuzha").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-16)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

### Relationships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Relationships")]

Thilakan's first partner was actress Santha with whom he appeared in several productions. Thilakan and Santha have three sons, Shaji, [Shammi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammi_Thilakan "Shammi Thilakan")&[Shobhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shobi_Thilakan "Shobi Thilakan"). Later, he had a second partner, his co-artist Sarojam with whom he had a son, Shibu Thilakan, and two daughters Dr. Sonia Thilakan and Sophia Ajith.

His grandson Abhimanyu made his debut in [Marco (2024)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_(2024_film) "Marco (2024 film)") starring [Unni Mukundan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unni_Mukundan "Unni Mukundan").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-17)

### Views

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Views")]

Thilakan was an [atheist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheist "Atheist")[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-18) throughout his life, and was a supporter of [Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party "Communist Party"). He was a member of many drama troupes which actively promoted Communism in Kerala. When he died, his dead body was draped with [Communist flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_symbolism "Communist symbolism").

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Death")]

For a long time, Thilakan dealt with numerous health issues like [diabetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabetes "Diabetes"), [hypertension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypertension "Hypertension") and [heart disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_disease "Heart disease"). He was hospitalized multiple times due to these problems. Finally, he was admitted to [Jubilee Mission Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jubilee_Mission_Hospital "Jubilee Mission Hospital") in [Thrissur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrissur "Thrissur") on 1 August 2012 after he collapsed during the shooting of the film _[Scene Onnu Nammude Veedu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scene\_Onnu\_Nammude\_Veedu "Scene Onnu Nammude Veedu")_. He was then shifted to KIMS Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram, and was in critical condition after suffering two heart attacks. Besides having cardiac problems, Thilakan was suffering from pneumonia. He was put on a ventilator and died on 24 September 2012.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-19) He was cremated with full state honours.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-20)

**Aranmula** is a temple town located in [Pathanamthitta district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathanamthitta_district "Pathanamthitta district") in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), India.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-2)

## Temples

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aranmula&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Temples")]

The [Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula_Parthasarathy_Temple "Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple") is one of the major temples in Kerala and has a great antiquity. It is one of the venerated [108 Vaishnava temples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divya_Desam "Divya Desam") in India and finds mention in Tamil classics. Spread over a vast area, the temple is on the banks of the Pampa and the whole temple complex is at a high elevation. Main idol is of Lord Krishna, who is the charioteer of warrior Arjuna in [Kurukshetra War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurukshetra_War "Kurukshetra War"). The temple has a flight of 18 steps that lead to the Eastern Tower while 57 descending steps from the Northern tower reaches the Pampa. The temple here has fine murals from the 18th century."Thanka Anki", the golden ornaments of Lord Ayyappa at Sabarimala is kept in Aranmula sri parthasarathy temple.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-3)

## Aranmula Panchayat

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aranmula&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Aranmula Panchayat")]

Shija T Toji was the president of the panchayat while N S Kumar was the vice-president from 2020 to 2025. The new president and vice-president will take charge following election in December 2025.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-4)

## Environmental Movements

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aranmula&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Environmental Movements")]

The Ministry of Civil Aviation of the Government of India has issued a letter dated 25 May 2015 withdrawing the 'in-principle' approval to the proposed Aranmula Airport Project.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-5) The Civil Aviation Ministry has also forwarded copies of the letter withdrawing the approval for the airport project to the Prime Minister's Office, Rashtrapathi Bhavan, Ministry of Home Affairs, Defence Ministry, Planning Commission, Departments of Economic Affairs and Revenue, and the Project Monitoring Group at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi. Prior to this, on 8 May 2015, the Ministry of Defence withdrew the No Objection Certificate (NOC) to the project. Earlier, on 28 May 2014, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) had cancelled the environment clearance granted to the project by the Union Ministry of Environment and Forests.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-6)

**Aranmula** is a temple town located in [Pathanamthitta district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathanamthitta_district "Pathanamthitta district") in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), India.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-2)

## Temples

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aranmula&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Temples")]

The [Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula_Parthasarathy_Temple "Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple") is one of the major temples in Kerala and has a great antiquity. It is one of the venerated [108 Vaishnava temples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divya_Desam "Divya Desam") in India and finds mention in Tamil classics. Spread over a vast area, the temple is on the banks of the Pampa and the whole temple complex is at a high elevation. Main idol is of Lord Krishna, who is the charioteer of warrior Arjuna in [Kurukshetra War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurukshetra_War "Kurukshetra War"). The temple has a flight of 18 steps that lead to the Eastern Tower while 57 descending steps from the Northern tower reaches the Pampa. The temple here has fine murals from the 18th century."Thanka Anki", the golden ornaments of Lord Ayyappa at Sabarimala is kept in Aranmula sri parthasarathy temple.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-3)

## Aranmula Panchayat

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aranmula&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Aranmula Panchayat")]

Shija T Toji was the president of the panchayat while N S Kumar was the vice-president from 2020 to 2025. The new president and vice-president will take charge following election in December 2025.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-4)

## Environmental Movements

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Aranmula&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Environmental Movements")]

The Ministry of Civil Aviation of the Government of India has issued a letter dated 25 May 2015 withdrawing the 'in-principle' approval to the proposed Aranmula Airport Project.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-5) The Civil Aviation Ministry has also forwarded copies of the letter withdrawing the approval for the airport project to the Prime Minister's Office, Rashtrapathi Bhavan, Ministry of Home Affairs, Defence Ministry, Planning Commission, Departments of Economic Affairs and Revenue, and the Project Monitoring Group at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi. Prior to this, on 8 May 2015, the Ministry of Defence withdrew the No Objection Certificate (NOC) to the project. Earlier, on 28 May 2014, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) had cancelled the environment clearance granted to the project by the Union Ministry of Environment and Forests.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranmula#cite_note-6)

**Palappurathu Keshavan Surendranatha Thilakan** (15 July 1935 – 24 September 2012), known mononymously as **Thilakan**, was an Indian film and stage actor who appeared in over 200 [Malayalam films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_films "Malayalam films").[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-2)[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-3)[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-4) Spanning more than five decades, Thilakan’s acting career was marked by critical acclaim for his versatility and powerful screen presence. He won several major honours including the [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") (2009) from the Government of India, multiple [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") and numerous [Kerala State Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Awards "Kerala State Film Awards"),[[5]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-5) becoming the most frequent winner of the [Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Award_for_Second_Best_Actor "Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor").

Thilakan was known for his elaborate method acting and realistic, spontaneous performances[[6]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-6) and is widely regarded as one of the greatest actors in Indian cinema, whose style influenced generations of Malayalam actors and audience.

## Early life

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Thilakan was the second of the six children of P. T. S. Keshavan of the Palappurathu house (1904–1972) and Devayani Amma (1912–2010). Thilakan was born in [Ayroor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayroor "Ayroor"), in the present-day [Pathanamthitta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathanamthitta "Pathanamthitta") district of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"). He had his primary education from Asan Pallikoodam, [Manikkal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manikkal "Manikkal") and St. Louis Catholic School, Nalamvayal, M. T. Seminary School Kottayam and Sree Narayana College, [Kollam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam "Kollam").He served in military while Jawaharlal Nehru was the Prime minister before starting his acting career. Thilakan lived in Ayroor until he started acting in films for which he moved to [Trivandrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trivandrum "Trivandrum").

Thilakan started his full-time career in acting after leaving college in the year 1956. During this period he and several friends formed a drama troupe called the _Mundakayam Nataka Samithy_ in [Mundakayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundakayam "Mundakayam"), where his father was working as an estate supervisor. He worked with the [Kerala People's Arts Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_People's_Arts_Club "Kerala People's Arts Club") till 1966, followed by stints in [Kalidasa Kalakendram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalidasa_Kalakendram "Kalidasa Kalakendram"), Changanacherry Geetha, and [P. J. Antony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Antony "P. J. Antony")'s troupe. He also performed in several radio plays presented by [All India Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_India_Radio "All India Radio").

## Career

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Thilakan began his career in cinema with a role in the [P. J. Antony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Antony "P. J. Antony")-directed Malayalam movie _[Periyar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periyar\_(1973\_film) "Periyar (1973 film)")_ (1973). He then worked in _Gandharvakshetram_ and _[Ulkadal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oolkatal "Oolkatal")_ (1979). His first role as a lead character was as Kallu Varkey, a drunkard in _[Kolangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolangal\_(1981\_film) "Kolangal (1981 film)")_ (1981). Thilakan was awarded his first [Kerala State Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Awards "Kerala State Film Awards") in 1982 for his role in _[Yavanika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yavanika "Yavanika")_. He also won Kerala State Award for supporting actor in _[Yathra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yathra "Yathra")_ which also starred [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty").

In 1988, he received the [National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor") for his performance in _[Rithubhedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rithubhedam "Rithubhedam"),_ and again in 1994. In 1998, he won State awards for _[Santhanagopalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santhanagopalam "Santhanagopalam")_ and _[Gamanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamanam\_(1994\_film) "Gamanam (1994 film)")_. He was strongly favored[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-rediff1-7) to get another [National Film Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor") for his performance in the movie _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)"),_ but the award was given to [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") over Thilakan amidst suspicions of strong lobbying, as Amitabh had announced his retirement earlier that year.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-rediff1-7) The film _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_ was a milestone in Thilakan's career; in this film, he portrayed a helpless policeman silently watching the fate of his son, played by [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal"), who was corrupted by society's influences. In 1989 he performed in [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") starrer _[Mrugya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrugaya\_(1989\_film) "Mrugaya (1989 film)")_, in which his role of a Reverend Father Panangodan was well appreciated by critics and won him many accolades. In the 1990s Thilakan was part of many [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") and [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal") evergreen hit films. In 1987, he was appreciated for his role in _[Thaniyavarthanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thaniyavarthanam "Thaniyavarthanam")_ where he portrayed a man who is the head of a family where his nephew played by Mammootty becomes lunatic due to superstition and lack of awareness of mental health. He was awarded the [Second Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Award_for_Second_Best_Actor "Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor") for _[Thaniyavarthanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thaniyavarthanam "Thaniyavarthanam")_. In the same year, he also played the comic role of _Ananthan Nambiar_ in the cult-classic comedy movie _[Nadodikkattu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadodikkattu "Nadodikkattu")_, from which several of Thilakan's lines became very popular. He also starred in the National award winning movie _[Mathilukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathilukal "Mathilukal")_, which was directed by [Adoor Gopalakrishnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adoor_Gopalakrishnan "Adoor Gopalakrishnan") in which he played the role of a warden of the jail who develops a rapport with the prisoner [Vaikom Muhammad Basheer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom_Muhammad_Basheer "Vaikom Muhammad Basheer") (Mammootty). In 1993, he continued his role as the father of Sethu Madhavan (Mohanlal) in the movie _[Chenkol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chenkol "Chenkol")_. Like its prequel _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_, this movie also fared well both commercially and critically. His role as a retired mathematics teacher and headmaster C.P Chacko alias Kaduva Chacko, father of Thomas Chacko alias Aadu Thoma (Mohanlal), in the 1995 blockbuster movie _[Spadikam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spadikam "Spadikam")_ was well appreciated by critics and audiences alike. In 1998, he played the role of Dileep's father in the superhit _[Meenathil Thalikettu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenathil\_Thalikettu "Meenathil Thalikettu")_, and in his subsequent release he donned the role of a villain in the Kunchako Boban starrer _[Mayilpeelikavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayilpeelikkavu "Mayilpeelikkavu")_. In the same year, he was also seen in _[Chinthavishtayaya Shyamala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinthavishtayaya\_Shyamala "Chinthavishtayaya Shyamala")_. Other notable films Thilakan has acted in include _[Yathra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yathra "Yathra")_, _[Mukthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukthi "Mukthi")_, _[Kauravar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kauravar "Kauravar")_, _[Moonnam Pakkam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonnam\_Pakkam "Moonnam Pakkam")_, _[Kilukkam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilukkam "Kilukkam")_, _[Namukku Parkkan Munthiri Thoppukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namukku\_Parkkan\_Munthiri\_Thoppukal "Namukku Parkkan Munthiri Thoppukal")_, _[Mookkilla Rajyathu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mookilla\_Rajyathu "Mookilla Rajyathu")_, _[Randam Bhavam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randam\_Bhavam "Randam Bhavam")_, _[Kaattu Kuthira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattukuthira "Kattukuthira")_ and _[Yavanika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yavanika "Yavanika")_.

He has also acted in other South Indian languages, such as [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_cinema "Tamil cinema"), [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") and [Kannada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannada "Kannada").

Thilakan has portrayed a range of characters; however, his most well-known role is that of the father of [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal"), portraying a father-son duo. Movies where he donned this role include _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_, _[Spadikam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphadikam "Sphadikam")_, _[Narasimham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narasimham\_(film) "Narasimham (film)")_, _[Evidam Swargamanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evidam\_Swargamanu "Evidam Swargamanu")_, _[Pavithram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavithram\_(1994\_film) "Pavithram (1994 film)")_ and _Chenkol_. He has also played father roles to other popular actors, including with [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") in _[Sangham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangham\_(1988\_film) "Sangham (1988 film)")_, _[The Truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Truth\_(1998\_film) "The Truth (1998 film)")_, _[Oliyampukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliyampukal "Oliyampukal")_, _[No. 1 Snehatheeram Bangalore North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No.\_1\_Snehatheeram\_Bangalore\_North "No. 1 Snehatheeram Bangalore North")_ and _[Pallavur Devanarayanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallavur\_Devanarayanan "Pallavur Devanarayanan")_, with [Jayaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayaram "Jayaram") in _[Veendum Chila Veettu Karyangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veendum\_Chila\_Veettukaryangal "Veendum Chila Veettukaryangal")_ and _[Sandesam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandhesam "Sandhesam")_, with [Kunchacko Boban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunchacko_Boban "Kunchacko Boban") in _[Aniyathi Pravu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aniyathi\_Pravu "Aniyathi Pravu")_, with [Dileep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dileep "Dileep") in _[Punjabi House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi\_House "Punjabi House")_ and _[Meenathil Thalikettu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenathil\_Thalikettu "Meenathil Thalikettu")_ and with [Prithviraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithviraj_Sukumaran "Prithviraj Sukumaran") in _[Sathyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sathyam\_(2004\_film) "Sathyam (2004 film)")_. He has also played a number of antagonists, such as in _[Randam Bhavam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randam\_Bhavam "Randam Bhavam")_, _Karma_ and _[Kaalal Pada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaalal\_Pada "Kaalal Pada")_. He has played comical roles in films like _[Nadodikkattu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadodikkattu "Nadodikkattu")_ and _[Pattanapravesham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattanapravesham "Pattanapravesham")_ (as a coward underworld don), _[Mookkilla Rajyathu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mookilla\_Rajyathu "Mookilla Rajyathu")_ (as a break-out from a mental hospital), _[Kuttettan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuttettan "Kuttettan")_ (as a pimp) and _[Naaduvazhikal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naduvazhikal "Naduvazhikal")_ (as a good-for-nothing, vain person). He is also remembered for the role of comic underworld don _Damodarjj_ in [Sanmanassullavarkku Samadhanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanmanassullavarkku_Samadhanam "Sanmanassullavarkku Samadhanam"). Thilakan played lead roles in _[Ekantham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eakantham "Eakantham")_, _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)")_, _[Santhanagopalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santhanagopalam "Santhanagopalam")_, _[Kaattukuthira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattukuthira "Kattukuthira")_, _[My Dear Muthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Dear\_Muthachan "My Dear Muthachan")_, _Mukhamudra_ (double role), etc.

In 2007, he acted in _[Ekantham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eakantham "Eakantham")_, for which he received a special mention from the jury.[[8]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-8) In 2009, he was also seen in [Pazhassi Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_Varma_Pazhassi_Raja_(film) "Kerala Varma Pazhassi Raja (film)"), and in the same year he played [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal")'s father one last time in the actor's 300th movie _[Evidam Swargamanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evidam\_Swargamanu "Evidam Swargamanu")_. In 2011, he played a significant role in the [Prithviraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithviraj_Sukumaran "Prithviraj Sukumaran") blockbuster _[Indian Rupee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian\_Rupee\_(film) "Indian Rupee (film)")_ directed by [Renjith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renjith "Renjith"). In 2012, he played the role of Kareem Bhai in _[Ustad Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ustad\_Hotel "Ustad Hotel")_ and as the grandfather of Faizy, acted by [Dulquer Salmaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulquer_Salmaan "Dulquer Salmaan").

## Controversies

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Controversies")]

### National Film Award

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: National Film Award")]

Thilakan, in an interview, claimed that the then jury chairman Ashok Kumar was keen on giving him the [1991 National Film Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_National_Film_Awards "39th National Film Awards") for [Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor") for _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)")_ but that a [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") leader wanted the award to be given to [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") to woo him back to their party.[[9]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-9)

### FEFKA

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: FEFKA")]

In February 2010, it was reported that the producer of the movie _[Christian Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian\_Brothers\_(film) "Christian Brothers (film)")_ excluded Thilakan from the film at the request of the [Film Employees Federation of Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_Employees_Federation_of_Kerala "Film Employees Federation of Kerala") (FEFKA), the predominant film technicians association. Thilakan had been earlier signed for a role in the film. The exclusion was reportedly due to Thilakan acting in a film by director [Vinayan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinayan "Vinayan"), who till recently headed the rival association MACTA. On 3 February 2010, Thilakan publicly protested against the unofficial ban enforced on him by FEFKA and blamed FEFKA for engineering the ban. The [Association of Malayalam Movie Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Malayalam_Movie_Artists "Association of Malayalam Movie Artists") (AMMA) issued a show cause notice to Thilakan for bringing the issue into the public domain. Thilakan accused AMMA, of which he too is a member.[[10]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-10)[[11]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-11) On 20 February 2010 the [CPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India "Communist Party of India")'s trade union wing, [AITUC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AITUC "AITUC"), came out openly in support of Thilakan, while a senior party leader and [Rajya Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajya_Sabha "Rajya Sabha") member [K. E. Ismail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._E._Ismail "K. E. Ismail") expressed reservations about political involvement in the issue.[[12]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-12)

Thilakan was originally cast to play a role in a UAE-Indian co-production film _[Dam 999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam\_999 "Dam 999")_.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-13) He was later replaced following a notice from FEFKA stating that the association would boycott the film if Thilakan were to act. Sohan, the director, was forced to seek a substitute for Thilakan when it "came to the point that shooting might be disrupted."[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-14) Eventually, [Rajit Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajit_Kapur "Rajit Kapur") was cast instead of Thilakan.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-amma-15) Some reports contended that Association of Malayalam Movie Artists (AMMA) also had intervened in Thilakan's replacement.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-amma-15) In response, Thilakan and his supporters orchestrated a march near the shooting location of the film in [Alappuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alappuzha "Alappuzha").[[16]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-16)

## Personal life

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

### Relationships

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Relationships")]

Thilakan's first partner was actress Santha with whom he appeared in several productions. Thilakan and Santha have three sons, Shaji, [Shammi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammi_Thilakan "Shammi Thilakan")&[Shobhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shobi_Thilakan "Shobi Thilakan"). Later, he had a second partner, his co-artist Sarojam with whom he had a son, Shibu Thilakan, and two daughters Dr. Sonia Thilakan and Sophia Ajith.

His grandson Abhimanyu made his debut in [Marco (2024)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_(2024_film) "Marco (2024 film)") starring [Unni Mukundan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unni_Mukundan "Unni Mukundan").[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-17)

### Views

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Views")]

Thilakan was an [atheist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheist "Atheist")[[18]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-18) throughout his life, and was a supporter of [Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party "Communist Party"). He was a member of many drama troupes which actively promoted Communism in Kerala. When he died, his dead body was draped with [Communist flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_symbolism "Communist symbolism").

## Death

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Death")]

For a long time, Thilakan dealt with numerous health issues like [diabetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabetes "Diabetes"), [hypertension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypertension "Hypertension") and [heart disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_disease "Heart disease"). He was hospitalized multiple times due to these problems. Finally, he was admitted to [Jubilee Mission Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jubilee_Mission_Hospital "Jubilee Mission Hospital") in [Thrissur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrissur "Thrissur") on 1 August 2012 after he collapsed during the shooting of the film _[Scene Onnu Nammude Veedu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scene\_Onnu\_Nammude\_Veedu "Scene Onnu Nammude Veedu")_. He was then shifted to KIMS Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram, and was in critical condition after suffering two heart attacks. Besides having cardiac problems, Thilakan was suffering from pneumonia. He was put on a ventilator and died on 24 September 2012.[[19]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-19) He was cremated with full state honours.[[20]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-20)

Indian actor

In this [Indian name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_name "Indian name"), the name _Palappurathu Keshavan_ is a [patronymic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), and the person should be referred to by the [given name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Given_name "Given name"), _Surendranatha Thilakan or Thilakan_.

**Palappurathu Keshavan Surendranatha Thilakan** (15 July 1935 – 24 September 2012), known mononymously as **Thilakan**, was an Indian film and stage actor who appeared in over 200 [Malayalam films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_films "Malayalam films").[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-2)[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-3)[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-4) Spanning more than five decades, Thilakan’s acting career was marked by critical acclaim for his versatility and powerful screen presence. He won several major honours including the [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") (2009) from the Government of India, multiple [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") and numerous [Kerala State Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Awards "Kerala State Film Awards"),[[5]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-5) becoming the most frequent winner of the [Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Award_for_Second_Best_Actor "Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor").

Thilakan was known for his elaborate method acting and realistic, spontaneous performances[[6]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-6) and is widely regarded as one of the greatest actors in Indian cinema, whose style influenced generations of Malayalam actors and audience.

## Early life

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Thilakan was the second of the six children of P. T. S. Keshavan of the Palappurathu house (1904–1972) and Devayani Amma (1912–2010). Thilakan was born in [Ayroor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayroor "Ayroor"), in the present-day [Pathanamthitta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathanamthitta "Pathanamthitta") district of [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"). He had his primary education from Asan Pallikoodam, [Manikkal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manikkal "Manikkal") and St. Louis Catholic School, Nalamvayal, M. T. Seminary School Kottayam and Sree Narayana College, [Kollam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kollam "Kollam").He served in military while Jawaharlal Nehru was the Prime minister before starting his acting career. Thilakan lived in Ayroor until he started acting in films for which he moved to [Trivandrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trivandrum "Trivandrum").

Thilakan started his full-time career in acting after leaving college in the year 1956. During this period he and several friends formed a drama troupe called the _Mundakayam Nataka Samithy_ in [Mundakayam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundakayam "Mundakayam"), where his father was working as an estate supervisor. He worked with the [Kerala People's Arts Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_People's_Arts_Club "Kerala People's Arts Club") till 1966, followed by stints in [Kalidasa Kalakendram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalidasa_Kalakendram "Kalidasa Kalakendram"), Changanacherry Geetha, and [P. J. Antony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Antony "P. J. Antony")'s troupe. He also performed in several radio plays presented by [All India Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_India_Radio "All India Radio").

## Career

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Thilakan began his career in cinema with a role in the [P. J. Antony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Antony "P. J. Antony")-directed Malayalam movie _[Periyar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periyar\_(1973\_film) "Periyar (1973 film)")_ (1973). He then worked in _Gandharvakshetram_ and _[Ulkadal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oolkatal "Oolkatal")_ (1979). His first role as a lead character was as Kallu Varkey, a drunkard in _[Kolangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolangal\_(1981\_film) "Kolangal (1981 film)")_ (1981). Thilakan was awarded his first [Kerala State Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Awards "Kerala State Film Awards") in 1982 for his role in _[Yavanika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yavanika "Yavanika")_. He also won Kerala State Award for supporting actor in _[Yathra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yathra "Yathra")_ which also starred [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty").

In 1988, he received the [National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor") for his performance in _[Rithubhedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rithubhedam "Rithubhedam"),_ and again in 1994. In 1998, he won State awards for _[Santhanagopalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santhanagopalam "Santhanagopalam")_ and _[Gamanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamanam\_(1994\_film) "Gamanam (1994 film)")_. He was strongly favored[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-rediff1-7) to get another [National Film Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor") for his performance in the movie _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)"),_ but the award was given to [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") over Thilakan amidst suspicions of strong lobbying, as Amitabh had announced his retirement earlier that year.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-rediff1-7) The film _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_ was a milestone in Thilakan's career; in this film, he portrayed a helpless policeman silently watching the fate of his son, played by [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal"), who was corrupted by society's influences. In 1989 he performed in [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") starrer _[Mrugya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrugaya\_(1989\_film) "Mrugaya (1989 film)")_, in which his role of a Reverend Father Panangodan was well appreciated by critics and won him many accolades. In the 1990s Thilakan was part of many [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") and [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal") evergreen hit films. In 1987, he was appreciated for his role in _[Thaniyavarthanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thaniyavarthanam "Thaniyavarthanam")_ where he portrayed a man who is the head of a family where his nephew played by Mammootty becomes lunatic due to superstition and lack of awareness of mental health. He was awarded the [Second Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_State_Film_Award_for_Second_Best_Actor "Kerala State Film Award for Second Best Actor") for _[Thaniyavarthanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thaniyavarthanam "Thaniyavarthanam")_. In the same year, he also played the comic role of _Ananthan Nambiar_ in the cult-classic comedy movie _[Nadodikkattu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadodikkattu "Nadodikkattu")_, from which several of Thilakan's lines became very popular. He also starred in the National award winning movie _[Mathilukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathilukal "Mathilukal")_, which was directed by [Adoor Gopalakrishnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adoor_Gopalakrishnan "Adoor Gopalakrishnan") in which he played the role of a warden of the jail who develops a rapport with the prisoner [Vaikom Muhammad Basheer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom_Muhammad_Basheer "Vaikom Muhammad Basheer") (Mammootty). In 1993, he continued his role as the father of Sethu Madhavan (Mohanlal) in the movie _[Chenkol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chenkol "Chenkol")_. Like its prequel _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_, this movie also fared well both commercially and critically. His role as a retired mathematics teacher and headmaster C.P Chacko alias Kaduva Chacko, father of Thomas Chacko alias Aadu Thoma (Mohanlal), in the 1995 blockbuster movie _[Spadikam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spadikam "Spadikam")_ was well appreciated by critics and audiences alike. In 1998, he played the role of Dileep's father in the superhit _[Meenathil Thalikettu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenathil\_Thalikettu "Meenathil Thalikettu")_, and in his subsequent release he donned the role of a villain in the Kunchako Boban starrer _[Mayilpeelikavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayilpeelikkavu "Mayilpeelikkavu")_. In the same year, he was also seen in _[Chinthavishtayaya Shyamala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinthavishtayaya\_Shyamala "Chinthavishtayaya Shyamala")_. Other notable films Thilakan has acted in include _[Yathra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yathra "Yathra")_, _[Mukthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukthi "Mukthi")_, _[Kauravar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kauravar "Kauravar")_, _[Moonnam Pakkam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonnam\_Pakkam "Moonnam Pakkam")_, _[Kilukkam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilukkam "Kilukkam")_, _[Namukku Parkkan Munthiri Thoppukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namukku\_Parkkan\_Munthiri\_Thoppukal "Namukku Parkkan Munthiri Thoppukal")_, _[Mookkilla Rajyathu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mookilla\_Rajyathu "Mookilla Rajyathu")_, _[Randam Bhavam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randam\_Bhavam "Randam Bhavam")_, _[Kaattu Kuthira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattukuthira "Kattukuthira")_ and _[Yavanika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yavanika "Yavanika")_.

He has also acted in other South Indian languages, such as [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_cinema "Tamil cinema"), [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") and [Kannada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannada "Kannada").

Thilakan has portrayed a range of characters; however, his most well-known role is that of the father of [Mohanlal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohanlal "Mohanlal"), portraying a father-son duo. Movies where he donned this role include _[Kireedam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kireedam\_(1989\_film) "Kireedam (1989 film)")_, _[Spadikam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphadikam "Sphadikam")_, _[Narasimham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narasimham\_(film) "Narasimham (film)")_, _[Evidam Swargamanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evidam\_Swargamanu "Evidam Swargamanu")_, _[Pavithram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavithram\_(1994\_film) "Pavithram (1994 film)")_ and _Chenkol_. He has also played father roles to other popular actors, including with [Mammootty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammootty "Mammootty") in _[Sangham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangham\_(1988\_film) "Sangham (1988 film)")_, _[The Truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Truth\_(1998\_film) "The Truth (1998 film)")_, _[Oliyampukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliyampukal "Oliyampukal")_, _[No. 1 Snehatheeram Bangalore North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No.\_1\_Snehatheeram\_Bangalore\_North "No. 1 Snehatheeram Bangalore North")_ and _[Pallavur Devanarayanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallavur\_Devanarayanan "Pallavur Devanarayanan")_, with [Jayaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayaram "Jayaram") in _[Veendum Chila Veettu Karyangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veendum\_Chila\_Veettukaryangal "Veendum Chila Veettukaryangal")_ and _[Sandesam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandhesam "Sandhesam")_, with [Kunchacko Boban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunchacko_Boban "Kunchacko Boban") in _[Aniyathi Pravu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aniyathi\_Pravu "Aniyathi Pravu")_, with [Dileep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dileep "Dileep") in _[Punjabi House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi\_House "Punjabi House")_ and _[Meenathil Thalikettu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenathil\_Thalikettu "Meenathil Thalikettu")_ and with [Prithviraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithviraj_Sukumaran "Prithviraj Sukumaran") in _[Sathyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sathyam\_(2004\_film) "Sathyam (2004 film)")_. He has also played a number of antagonists, such as in _[Randam Bhavam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randam\_Bhavam "Randam Bhavam")_, _Karma_ and _[Kaalal Pada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaalal\_Pada "Kaalal Pada")_. He has played comical roles in films like _[Nadodikkattu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadodikkattu "Nadodikkattu")_ and _[Pattanapravesham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pattanapravesham "Pattanapravesham")_ (as a coward underworld don), _[Mookkilla Rajyathu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mookilla\_Rajyathu "Mookilla Rajyathu")_ (as a break-out from a mental hospital), _[Kuttettan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuttettan "Kuttettan")_ (as a pimp) and _[Naaduvazhikal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naduvazhikal "Naduvazhikal")_ (as a good-for-nothing, vain person). He is also remembered for the role of comic underworld don _Damodarjj_ in [Sanmanassullavarkku Samadhanam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanmanassullavarkku_Samadhanam "Sanmanassullavarkku Samadhanam"). Thilakan played lead roles in _[Ekantham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eakantham "Eakantham")_, _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)")_, _[Santhanagopalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santhanagopalam "Santhanagopalam")_, _[Kaattukuthira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattukuthira "Kattukuthira")_, _[My Dear Muthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Dear\_Muthachan "My Dear Muthachan")_, _Mukhamudra_ (double role), etc.

## Controversies

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Controversies")]

### National Film Award

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: National Film Award")]

Thilakan, in an interview, claimed that the then jury chairman Ashok Kumar was keen on giving him the [1991 National Film Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_National_Film_Awards "39th National Film Awards") for [Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor") for _[Perumthachan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perumthachan\_(film) "Perumthachan (film)")_ but that a [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") leader wanted the award to be given to [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") to woo him back to their party.[[9]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-9)

### FEFKA

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: FEFKA")]

In February 2010, it was reported that the producer of the movie _[Christian Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian\_Brothers\_(film) "Christian Brothers (film)")_ excluded Thilakan from the film at the request of the [Film Employees Federation of Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_Employees_Federation_of_Kerala "Film Employees Federation of Kerala") (FEFKA), the predominant film technicians association. Thilakan had been earlier signed for a role in the film. The exclusion was reportedly due to Thilakan acting in a film by director [Vinayan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinayan "Vinayan"), who till recently headed the rival association MACTA. On 3 February 2010, Thilakan publicly protested against the unofficial ban enforced on him by FEFKA and blamed FEFKA for engineering the ban. The [Association of Malayalam Movie Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Malayalam_Movie_Artists "Association of Malayalam Movie Artists") (AMMA) issued a show cause notice to Thilakan for bringing the issue into the public domain. Thilakan accused AMMA, of which he too is a member.[[10]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-10)[[11]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-11) On 20 February 2010 the [CPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India "Communist Party of India")'s trade union wing, [AITUC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AITUC "AITUC"), came out openly in support of Thilakan, while a senior party leader and [Rajya Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajya_Sabha "Rajya Sabha") member [K. E. Ismail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._E._Ismail "K. E. Ismail") expressed reservations about political involvement in the issue.[[12]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-12)

Thilakan was originally cast to play a role in a UAE-Indian co-production film _[Dam 999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam\_999 "Dam 999")_.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-13) He was later replaced following a notice from FEFKA stating that the association would boycott the film if Thilakan were to act. Sohan, the director, was forced to seek a substitute for Thilakan when it "came to the point that shooting might be disrupted."[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-14) Eventually, [Rajit Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajit_Kapur "Rajit Kapur") was cast instead of Thilakan.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-amma-15) Some reports contended that Association of Malayalam Movie Artists (AMMA) also had intervened in Thilakan's replacement.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-amma-15) In response, Thilakan and his supporters orchestrated a march near the shooting location of the film in [Alappuzha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alappuzha "Alappuzha").[[16]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-16)

## Personal life

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

### Relationships

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Relationships")]

Thilakan's first partner was actress Santha with whom he appeared in several productions. Thilakan and Santha have three sons, Shaji, [Shammi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammi_Thilakan "Shammi Thilakan")&[Shobhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shobi_Thilakan "Shobi Thilakan"). Later, he had a second partner, his co-artist Sarojam with whom he had a son, Shibu Thilakan, and two daughters Dr. Sonia Thilakan and Sophia Ajith.

His grandson Abhimanyu made his debut in [Marco (2024)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_(2024_film) "Marco (2024 film)") starring [Unni Mukundan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unni_Mukundan "Unni Mukundan").[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-17)

### Views

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Views")]

Thilakan was an [atheist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheist "Atheist")[[18]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-18) throughout his life, and was a supporter of [Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party "Communist Party"). He was a member of many drama troupes which actively promoted Communism in Kerala. When he died, his dead body was draped with [Communist flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_symbolism "Communist symbolism").

## Death

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Thilakan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Death")]

For a long time, Thilakan dealt with numerous health issues like [diabetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabetes "Diabetes"), [hypertension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypertension "Hypertension") and [heart disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_disease "Heart disease"). He was hospitalized multiple times due to these problems. Finally, he was admitted to [Jubilee Mission Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jubilee_Mission_Hospital "Jubilee Mission Hospital") in [Thrissur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrissur "Thrissur") on 1 August 2012 after he collapsed during the shooting of the film _[Scene Onnu Nammude Veedu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scene\_Onnu\_Nammude\_Veedu "Scene Onnu Nammude Veedu")_. He was then shifted to KIMS Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram, and was in critical condition after suffering two heart attacks. Besides having cardiac problems, Thilakan was suffering from pneumonia. He was put on a ventilator and died on 24 September 2012.[[19]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-19) He was cremated with full state honours.[[20]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thilakan#cite_note-20)
